title: Mutual Fund Distributors
blurb: The licence to distribute mutual funds in India. Twelve units, taught as concepts, examples and traps.

units.title: Concept and role of a mutual fund
units.overview: A mutual fund pools money from many investors and invests it in securities under professional management. Unit 1 builds the vocabulary everything else rests on: units, NAV, diversification and why a fund is not a guarantee.
focus: Why pooling gives small investors access to diversified portfolios.
How NAV changes and what it does not tell you.
The difference between a mutual fund and a bank deposit.
Types of funds by structure: open-ended, closed-ended, interval.
facts: Mutual fund
A mutual fund is a trust that pools money from many investors and invests it in securities such as shares and bonds, managed by professionals for the benefit of unit holders.
Two hundred small investors put in ₹5,000 each and one team invests the combined sum across many companies.
A mutual fund guarantees a fixed return to every investor.
Unit
A unit is the smallest share of a mutual fund scheme's portfolio that an investor owns. The number of units held shows the investor's proportional ownership.
An investor puts in ₹10,000 when the NAV is ₹20 and receives 500 of these.
Each unit always stays worth ₹10.
Net Asset Value (NAV)
NAV is the per-unit value of a scheme: total market value of its assets less its liabilities, divided by the number of units outstanding.
A scheme has assets of ₹520 crore, liabilities of ₹20 crore and 25 crore units, so this is ₹20.
A fund with a low NAV is cheaper and therefore a better buy.
Diversification
Diversification means spreading investments across many securities, sectors or asset classes so that a fall in one has a limited effect on the whole portfolio.
A scheme holds 50 stocks across many sectors, so one company's collapse barely moves its NAV.
Diversification removes all risk from a portfolio.
Professional management
Professional management means a qualified fund manager and research team select and monitor securities for the scheme, for a fee charged as part of the expense ratio.
An investor with no time for research relies on a team that tracks companies full time.
Professional management guarantees returns above the market.
Open-ended scheme
An open-ended scheme accepts purchases and redemptions at NAV on every business day after launch and has no fixed maturity.
An investor can buy more units or redeem on any working day long after the launch.
An open-ended scheme can be redeemed only on maturity.
Closed-ended scheme
A closed-ended scheme has a fixed maturity and units are bought during the NFO only; investors exit at maturity or by selling on a stock exchange where listed.
A scheme with a three-year maturity lets investors in only during the launch period.
A closed-ended scheme allows fresh purchases daily from the fund house.
Interval scheme
An interval scheme combines open and closed features: units can be bought or redeemed only during specified intervals, and units are listed on exchanges.
A scheme allows transactions only during two intervals each year.
An interval scheme lets investors transact on any day.
Risk in mutual funds
Mutual fund investments are subject to market risk. The value of units can rise and fall, and past performance does not assure future results.
An investor sees her equity fund fall 12% in a month during a market correction.
Mutual funds are as safe as a bank fixed deposit.
Liquidity
Liquidity in mutual funds means that units of open-ended schemes can be redeemed on any business day at the applicable NAV, subject to exit loads and settlement time.
An investor needs cash and redeems units of an open-ended scheme, receiving payment in a few working days.
All mutual fund units can be encashed instantly at any hour.
Transparency
Mutual funds disclose NAV daily, portfolios monthly and factsheets regularly, so investors can see where their money is invested.
An investor reads last month's portfolio holdings published by the fund house.
Fund houses are not required to publish their holdings.
Economies of scale
Economies of scale mean that large pooled funds can buy securities in bulk and spread costs, lowering per-unit costs for investors.
A big pooled fund pays lower dealing costs per rupee than a small individual investor.
Pooling increases the cost per unit for every investor.

units.title: Fund structure and constituents
units.overview: In India a mutual fund has a three-tier structure of sponsor, trust and asset management company, supported by service providers. This unit teaches who does what, and who checks whom.
focus: The role of the sponsor, trustees and AMC.
Custodian, registrar and transfer agent duties.
Why independence of trustees and directors matters.
facts: Sponsor
The sponsor is the person or entity that sets up the mutual fund and establishes the trust. It must meet SEBI's track-record and net-worth conditions.
A bank group creates a new fund house and registers its trust with SEBI.
The sponsor manages the investments of each scheme day to day.
Trustees
Trustees hold the fund's property in trust for unit holders and supervise the AMC. At least two-thirds of the trustees must be independent of the sponsor.
A board looks after investor interests and reviews the AMC's compliance reports.
Trustees decide which stocks the schemes buy.
Asset Management Company (AMC)
The AMC is appointed by the trustees to manage the schemes' investments and operations. At least half of its directors must be independent of the sponsor.
A company runs the fund's portfolios and employs the fund managers.
The AMC holds the securities of the schemes.
Custodian
The custodian safekeeps the securities and settles the trades of the schemes, and is independent of the sponsor.
An institution holds the scheme's shares in its safekeeping and handles delivery.
The custodian selects which securities the fund buys.
Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA)
The RTA maintains unit holders' records, processes purchases and redemptions, and sends statements on behalf of the AMC.
An agency updates investor folios and dispatches account statements.
The RTA calculates the portfolio's investment strategy.
Fund accountant and auditor
The fund accountant maintains the scheme's books and computes NAV, while auditors independently audit the accounts.
A firm prepares the scheme's accounts and an independent firm audits them.
The AMC may appoint the sponsor's auditor to the scheme.
Sponsor's contribution
The sponsor must contribute at least 40% of the net worth of the AMC.
A sponsor holds 40% of the AMC's net worth when the fund house is set up.
The sponsor need not contribute to the AMC's net worth.
Mutual fund as a trust
In India a mutual fund is constituted as a public trust under the Indian Trusts Act, and the trust is registered with SEBI.
A fund house sets up its mutual fund as a registered public trust.
A mutual fund in India is incorporated as a company.

units.title: Legal and regulatory environment
units.overview: Mutual funds are among the most regulated products in India. This unit covers SEBI, AMFI, the rules distributors must follow, the scheme categories, disclosures and investor grievance routes.
focus: SEBI's role and the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations.
AMFI, ARN, EUIN and the Code of Conduct.
visuals: Statutory regulator of mutual funds and the securities market
Industry body; issues ARN, sets Code of Conduct, publishes NAVs
Regulates banks and some money-market instruments
facts: SEBI
The Securities and Exchange Board of India is the statutory regulator that registers and regulates mutual funds and protects investors under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.
A fund house must obtain a certificate of registration before launching schemes.
AMFI is the statutory regulator of mutual funds.
AMFI
The Association of Mutual Funds in India is the industry body of AMCs. It sets best practices, issues the ARN to distributors, and publishes the daily NAVs.
A distributor applies for a registration number through the industry association.
AMFI makes the laws that bind mutual funds.
ARN
The AMFI Registration Number is a unique number issued to a distributor who has passed the NISM certification and follows the Code of Conduct. It must be renewed periodically.
A certified distributor quotes her unique registration number on every application.
A distributor needs no registration to sell mutual funds.
EUIN
The Employee Unique Identification Number identifies the individual employee or relationship manager who advises on a transaction, even when an ARN of the firm is used.
A bank's relationship manager's own code is entered on the investor's form.
An EUIN is allotted to every investor on investing.
Scheme categorisation
SEBI groups schemes into equity, debt, hybrid, solution oriented and other categories with defined definitions, and each AMC may offer only one scheme per category, with a few exceptions.
A fund house cannot launch two large-cap schemes that differ only in name.
AMCs can name and define scheme types as they like.
Riskometer
The riskometer shows a scheme's risk on six levels: low, low to moderate, moderate, moderately high, high and very high, and is updated based on portfolio risk.
A scheme's cover page displays a dial pointing to very high.
The riskometer has only three levels: low, medium and high.
Fundamental attribute change
A change in a scheme's fundamental attributes needs a written notice to unit holders and an exit option at the prevailing NAV without exit load for at least 30 days.
A fund house changes a scheme's investment objective and gives holders a window to leave free of exit load.
Fund houses can change fundamental attributes without informing investors.
Portfolio disclosure
Mutual funds publish portfolios of all schemes monthly on their websites and with AMFI, and publish the half-yearly financial results.
An investor checks last month's holdings on a fund house's site.
Portfolios are disclosed once a year only.
Cash investment limit
An investor can invest in cash in a mutual fund up to ₹50,000 per investor per mutual fund per financial year.
A person tries to invest ₹80,000 in cash in one fund house in a year.
There is no limit on investing in cash.
KYC
Know Your Customer is mandatory for all mutual fund investors. It verifies identity and address, and the records are kept with a KYC registration agency.
A first-time investor is asked for PAN, address proof and a photograph.
KYC is required only for investments above ₹10 lakh.
Stamp duty on units
Stamp duty is charged at 0.005% on the purchase of mutual fund units, including switches and SIP instalments.
An investor sees a tiny deduction at the time units are allotted.
Stamp duty is charged on units only when redeemed.
SEBI SCORES / ODR
Investors can file complaints against AMCs and intermediaries through SEBI's complaint system, and use the online dispute resolution platform if not satisfied.
A holder whose redemption was delayed lodges a complaint online with the regulator.
Complaints against AMCs can be made only to the sponsor.
Code of Conduct
AMFI's Code of Conduct requires distributors to act honestly, disclose commissions, give suitable advice, and not mislead investors.
A distributor tells the client the commission he earns on the scheme.
The Code of Conduct allows promising assured returns.
Product labelling
Each scheme's cover and advertisements must describe the product in plain language: what the scheme is, suited for whom, and what risk level applies.
A scheme's documents say it is suited to investors seeking long-term growth and carries very high risk.
Product labels are optional for equity schemes.

units.title: Offer document
units.overview: Before investing, an investor should read the scheme's offer document. This unit teaches the SID, SAI, NFO process and what each contains.
focus: SID, SAI and what each contains.
Where the scheme's risk factors, load and asset allocation are found.
facts: Scheme Information Document (SID)
The SID contains scheme-specific details: investment objective, asset allocation, strategy, risk factors, load structure, benchmark and fees.
An investor wants to know the scheme's asset allocation and exit load before investing.
The SID contains only the fund house's history.
Statement of Additional Information (SAI)
The SAI holds information common to the fund house and all its schemes: constitution, sponsor, trustees, AMC, service providers and legal details.
A reader wants the sponsor's and trustees' details, not any one scheme's.
The SAI contains details of only a single scheme.
Key Information Memorandum (KIM)

The KIM is a short summary of the SID and SAI given with the application form so investors see the essentials first. SEBI has since moved towards a standard scheme summary document with the same purpose.
A short summary document is attached to the application form.
The KIM replaces the need for any offer document.
New Fund Offer (NFO)
An NFO is the initial offer of a new scheme's units to the public. The offer period cannot exceed 15 days.
A fund house opens subscription for a newly launched scheme for two weeks.
An NFO can stay open for six months.
NFO price
Units in an NFO are typically offered at ₹10 each, with no assurance that this is a better price than existing schemes' NAV.
An investor assumes a ₹10 unit is cheaper than a ₹50 unit in another scheme.
A scheme at ₹10 is cheaper in value than one at ₹50.
Allotment timeline
Units must be allotted and refunds, if any, paid within five working days from the closure of the NFO.
The NFO closes and units are allotted a few working days later.
Allotment can be made after two months.
Asset allocation pattern
The SID states the proportion of the scheme's assets to be held in each asset class and the permissible ranges, which are binding on the fund manager.
A debt scheme's document says at least 80% will be in a certain type of paper.
The fund manager can ignore the stated asset allocation.
Scheme-specific risk factors
The offer document lists the risks specific to the scheme, such as credit risk for debt schemes, so that investors make informed decisions.
A debt fund's document warns about downgrade of issuers' ratings.
Risk factors are required only for equity schemes.

units.title: Fund distribution and channel management practices
units.overview: Distributors are the bridge between investors and AMCs. This unit covers channels, plans, commissions, mis-selling and the practices expected of a professional.
focus: Trail commission and how distributors are paid.
visuals: Paid to distributor from the scheme
facts: Direct plan
A direct plan is bought directly from the AMC without a distributor, so no commission is paid and the expense ratio is lower.
An investor buys directly from the fund house's website and pays no distributor commission.
A direct plan always earns higher returns than a regular plan in every period.
Regular plan
A regular plan is bought through a distributor, who is paid a commission from the scheme's expense ratio, making its expense ratio higher than the direct plan's.
An investor buys through an adviser who is paid from the scheme's costs.
A regular plan has the same expense ratio as the direct plan.
Trail commission
Trail commission is paid to a distributor as long as the investor stays invested, usually as a percentage of the assets he has brought in.
A distributor earns a small percentage every year on the client's holding.
Trail commission is paid only once, on the day of investing.
Upfront commission
SEBI has banned upfront commission to distributors; commissions are now paid on a trail basis, to align the distributor's interest with the investor's.
A distributor cannot take a lump sum at the time of purchase.
Distributors can still take a large upfront commission.
Mis-selling
Mis-selling is selling a product that is unsuitable for the client or by misrepresenting its features, risk or returns.
A distributor sells a high-risk equity fund to a retired client who needs safety by promising assured returns.
Mis-selling happens only when the product is illegal.
Churning
Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.
A distributor shifts a client's money between schemes every month without any reason.
Churning benefits the investor through lower costs.
Suitability
Suitability means recommending a product that fits the client's goals, risk profile, time horizon and financial situation.
A distributor checks a client's horizon and risk tolerance before suggesting a scheme.
Suitability is determined only by the scheme's past return.
Disclosure of commission
A distributor must disclose to the investor all commissions received from the AMC for the transaction, in a transparent manner.
A distributor tells the client how much she will earn on the recommended scheme.
Commissions are confidential and need not be disclosed.
Distributor channels
Mutual fund distribution channels include independent financial advisers, national distributors, banks, and online platforms and direct AMC routes.
A client may invest through a bank branch, an independent adviser or an app.
The only channel to buy mutual funds is a bank branch.
Segregation of roles
A person cannot be both a registered investment adviser and a distributor for the same client; roles and fees must be kept clearly separate to avoid conflicts of interest.
An adviser charging fees to a client cannot also earn distribution commission from the same client.
An adviser can charge a fee and also take commission from the same client.
Know Your Distributor
AMCs carry out due diligence on distributors and check that their ARN, certification and code compliance are valid before accepting business.
An AMC checks that the distributor's registration is valid before paying commission.
AMCs pay commissions without checking the distributor's registration.

units.title: Accounting, valuation and taxation
units.overview: How is NAV worked out, what costs are charged to investors, and how are gains taxed? This unit mixes formulas with rules and is heavily tested.
focus: NAV calculation and valuation of securities.
Taxation of equity, debt and hybrid funds.
visuals: NAV = (Market value of investments + other assets − liabilities and expenses) ÷ number of units outstanding
facts: NAV calculation
NAV equals the market value of the scheme's assets less its liabilities, divided by units outstanding, and is declared every business day.
A scheme's net assets are ₹1,000 crore and it has 50 crore units outstanding, so the value per unit is ₹20.
NAV is declared once a week.
Equity valuation
Listed equity shares are valued at the closing price on the principal stock exchange on the valuation day.
A scheme values its holding of a listed company at the exchange closing price.
Shares are valued at the price at which they were bought.
Debt valuation
Debt securities are valued at prices provided by SEBI-approved valuation agencies appointed by AMFI, to ensure uniform valuation across funds.
Two fund houses holding the same bond use the same price from an independent agency.
Each AMC values bonds as it sees fit.
Total expense ratio (TER)
TER is the annual percentage of a scheme's average assets charged for management, distribution and operating costs, and it is reflected in the daily NAV.
A scheme's NAV is net of annual running charges that fund investors never see as a bill.
TER is deducted separately from the investor's bank account.
Slab-wise TER
SEBI sets maximum TER slabs that fall as a scheme's assets under management grow, so larger schemes charge a lower percentage.
A very large scheme is permitted a lower maximum expense ratio than a small one.
The maximum TER rises as the scheme grows.
Exit load
Exit load is a charge levied when units are redeemed within a stated period. It is credited to the scheme, not kept by the AMC.
An investor redeems within a year and has 1% deducted from the proceeds, which is returned to the scheme.
Exit load is paid to the distributor.
Entry load
SEBI has abolished entry load; no fee can be deducted from the investor's money at the time of purchase.
An investor invests ₹10,000 and all of it is invested, with none deducted as load.
Entry load of 2.25% is still allowed on purchases.
STCG on equity funds
Gains on equity-oriented funds sold within 12 months are short-term and taxed at 20%.
An investor sells an equity fund after eight months and pays the short-term rate.
Short-term equity gains are exempt from tax.
LTCG on equity funds
Gains on equity-oriented funds held over 12 months are taxed at 12.5% on the amount above ₹1.25 lakh in a financial year.
An investor's long-term gain in a year is ₹3 lakh and only the portion above the exemption is taxed.
Long-term equity gains are taxed from the first rupee.
Equity-oriented fund
For tax purposes, an equity-oriented fund invests at least 65% of its assets in equity shares of domestic companies.
A scheme holding 70% in domestic shares qualifies for equity tax treatment.
A scheme with 40% equity is equity-oriented.
Specified mutual fund
A specified mutual fund invests more than 65% in debt and money-market instruments. Gains on units bought from April 2023 are taxed at the investor's slab rate regardless of holding period.
A debt fund bought in 2024 and held for four years is taxed at the investor's slab rate.
A debt fund held beyond three years gets indexation benefit.
IDCW taxation
Income distribution cum capital withdrawal payouts are added to the investor's income and taxed at the slab rate, with TDS where applicable.
An investor receives a dividend from a scheme and adds it to total income.
IDCW is tax-free in the hands of all investors.
STT
Securities Transaction Tax is levied on the redemption of equity-oriented fund units; there is no STT on purchase, and none on debt funds.
An investor sells equity fund units and a small tax is deducted on the sale value.
STT is charged on every purchase of mutual fund units.
Ex-dividend NAV effect
When an IDCW is paid, the scheme's NAV falls by the amount paid, so the investor's wealth is unchanged before tax.
A scheme pays ₹2 per unit and its NAV drops by ₹2 the same day.
IDCW is extra money that does not reduce NAV.

units.title: Investor service
units.overview: This is the practical heart of the exam: how transactions work. Cut-off times, applicable NAV, SIP, STP, SWP, nomination, transmission and statements are all in here.
focus: Nomination, joint holders, minors and transmission.
visuals: Equity/debt purchase, funds available before cut-off
Liquid and overnight purchase, funds available before cut-off
facts: Cut-off time
The cut-off time is the time of day by which a valid application with funds must be received to get that day's NAV. For most schemes it is 3:00 pm.
An investor submits an application at 2:30 pm with funds available and gets that day's NAV.
Applications received at 6 pm get the same day's NAV.
Applicable NAV
The NAV applied to a transaction depends on the cut-off time and when the funds are available for use by the scheme, not just when the application is made.
A purchase made before cut-off but with funds credited next day takes the later day's NAV.
The NAV applied is always the one on the day of the cheque.
SIP
A Systematic Investment Plan invests a fixed amount at regular intervals, which averages the purchase cost and builds discipline.
An investor invests ₹5,000 on the 5th of every month into the same scheme.
A SIP guarantees profit at the end of the term.
Rupee cost averaging
Rupee cost averaging means a fixed amount buys more units when NAV is low and fewer when it is high, lowering the average cost per unit over time.
A SIP buys more units during a fall in the market.
Rupee cost averaging ensures there will never be a loss.
STP
A Systematic Transfer Plan transfers a fixed amount at regular intervals from one scheme to another within the same fund house.
An investor moves ₹10,000 monthly from a liquid fund to an equity fund of the same AMC.
An STP moves money to the investor's bank account.
SWP
A Systematic Withdrawal Plan redeems a fixed amount of units at regular intervals, giving the investor a regular cash flow.
A retiree redeems units worth ₹20,000 on the first of every month for expenses.
An SWP is a plan to buy units regularly.
Switch
A switch is moving investment from one scheme to another, or between plans or options in the same scheme; it is treated as redemption and fresh purchase.
An investor shifts from a large-cap fund to a debt fund of the same AMC.
A switch has no tax or load implications.
Nomination
Nomination lets a holder name a person who will receive the units on the holder's death. Nominees are not the legal owners; they hold the proceeds for the legal heirs.
An investor names her spouse so the units pass on smoothly if she dies.
A nominee becomes the permanent legal owner of the units.
Joint holding modes
In 'anyone or survivor' mode, any holder can operate the folio; in 'joint', all must sign. On a holder's death the units go to the survivors.
A couple opens a folio where either can redeem alone.
In 'anyone or survivor' mode all holders must sign each redemption.
Minor investor
A minor's folio is operated by a guardian, and when the minor turns 18 a fresh KYC is needed, and the guardian's operation stops.
A father invests on behalf of his twelve-year-old daughter.
A minor can redeem without a guardian.
Lien
A lien is a charge marked on units, for example when pledged as security for a loan, so they cannot be redeemed until the lien is removed.
An investor's units are marked as security for a loan, and cannot be sold.
A lien means the units have been sold.
Transmission
Transmission is the transfer of units to the legal heirs or surviving holders on the death of a holder, supported by documents like the death certificate.
After the death of a sole holder, the nominee submits the death certificate to claim the units.
Transmission is the same as a switch.
Redemption timeline
Redemption proceeds must generally be paid within three working days of the transaction date for most schemes; liquid funds may be quicker.
An investor sells units today and expects to receive money in a few working days.
Redemption proceeds can take two months.
Consolidated Account Statement (CAS)
A single statement covering all of an investor's mutual fund holdings across AMCs, sent monthly if there were transactions, otherwise half-yearly.
An investor receives one statement showing all her funds from different fund houses.
The CAS covers only one fund house's schemes.
Demat mode
Mutual fund units can be held in dematerialised form with a depository participant, in addition to a statement of account from the AMC.
An investor holds units in the same account as her shares.
Mutual fund units can never be held in demat form.
Folio
A folio is the account number allotted by an AMC to an investor, under which all that investor's units in that fund house are recorded.
An investor quotes her account number with a fund house to check her units.
A folio is a type of scheme.
Dividend or IDCW payout timeline
Payout of IDCW must be dispatched within seven working days of the record date.
An investor expects IDCW proceeds a few days after the declared date.
IDCW can be dispatched any time within six months.
Change of bank details
A change of bank details needs a written request with proof of the new bank and is checked by the RTA; some schemes impose a cooling-off for large redemptions.
An investor updates the registered bank account with supporting proof.
Bank details cannot be changed after the first investment.

units.title: Return, risk and performance of funds
units.overview: Measuring what an investment has earned and at what risk. Unit 8 is where formulas such as CAGR, standard deviation, beta and Sharpe ratio live.
focus: Duration, yield to maturity and credit risk in debt funds.
visuals: Sharpe = (Portfolio return − Risk-free return) ÷ Standard deviation
facts: Absolute return
Absolute return is the percentage change in value over a period, ignoring how long it took. It is (end value − start value) ÷ start value.
A ₹10,000 investment grows to ₹12,000 in total, and the gain is expressed as 20%.
Absolute return already adjusts for the length of time.
CAGR
Compound Annual Growth Rate is the constant yearly rate at which an investment would have grown to reach its final value, used for periods over one year.
₹1 lakh becomes ₹1.21 lakh in two years, which is 10% a year compounded.
CAGR is the simple average of each year's return.
XIRR
XIRR is the annualised return when there are multiple cash flows on different dates, such as SIP instalments.
An investor wants the true annual return on a SIP made across many months.
XIRR can be used only for lump-sum investments.
Standard deviation
Standard deviation measures how much a fund's returns vary around its average. A higher figure means more volatility.
Two funds earn the same average return, but one swings far more from year to year.
A higher standard deviation means lower risk.
Beta
Beta measures a fund's sensitivity to the market. A beta of 1.2 means it is expected to move 20% more than the market.
A fund tends to rise 12% when the market rises 10%.
Beta measures the fund's absolute return.
Alpha
Alpha is the excess return of a fund over what its risk (beta) would predict, showing the value added by the fund manager.
A fund earns 3% more than a CAPM-based expectation for its risk.
A negative alpha shows outperformance.
Sharpe ratio
The Sharpe ratio is the excess return over the risk-free rate per unit of standard deviation. A higher ratio means better risk-adjusted performance.
Two funds have the same return, but one takes less volatility to achieve it and has the higher ratio.
The Sharpe ratio uses beta as its risk measure.
Tracking error
Tracking error is the standard deviation of the difference between an index fund's return and its benchmark's. A lower figure means closer replication.
An index fund drifts a little from its index return every year.
A high tracking error is desirable for index funds.
Total Return Index (TRI)
A TRI reflects both price changes and reinvested dividends of the index constituents, and is the proper benchmark for comparison with a fund's returns.
A fund's return is compared with an index that includes dividends.
A price index is the preferred benchmark because it includes dividends.
Modified duration
Modified duration estimates the percentage change in a bond's price for a 1% change in yield. A higher duration means more interest-rate sensitivity.
A bond fund with a duration of 5 falls about 5% if yields rise 1%.
Duration measures the credit rating of the bond.
Yield to maturity (YTM)
YTM is the annualised return earned if a bond is held to maturity and all coupons are reinvested at the same rate.
A bond's expected return if held until it matures is called its yield.
YTM is the coupon rate printed on the bond.
Credit risk
Credit risk is the chance that a bond issuer fails to pay interest or principal on time. Lower-rated issuers carry higher credit risk.
A fund holding a low-rated company's bonds suffers when the company defaults.
Government securities carry the highest credit risk.
Interest rate risk
When interest rates rise, the prices of existing bonds fall and vice versa, which affects debt fund NAVs, especially of longer-duration funds.
A long-duration gilt fund loses value when the central bank raises rates.
Bond prices rise when interest rates rise.
Risk-return trade-off
Higher potential return generally comes with higher risk. Investors who want higher returns must accept greater volatility.
An investor wanting equity-like returns must accept bigger swings in value.
High returns can be earned without any additional risk.
Liquidity risk
Liquidity risk is the chance a fund cannot sell securities quickly without a price discount, such as in thinly traded bonds.
A fund finds it hard to sell a bond that few people trade, except at a lower price.
Liquidity risk affects only equity funds.

units.title: Mutual fund scheme selection
units.overview: How to choose among thousands of schemes. This unit is mostly about SEBI's categories and what each is permitted to hold, plus the criteria a good distributor uses.
focus: Equity, debt, hybrid and solution-oriented categories.
facts: Large cap fund
A large cap fund invests at least 80% of its assets in the top 100 companies by market capitalisation.
A scheme holds 85% in the 100 biggest listed companies.
A large cap fund invests mainly in companies ranked 251 onwards.
Mid cap fund
A mid cap fund invests at least 65% in companies ranked 101 to 250 by market capitalisation.
A scheme keeps 70% in stocks ranked 101 to 250.
A mid cap fund invests mainly in the top 100 companies.
Small cap fund
A small cap fund invests at least 65% in companies ranked 251 and below by market capitalisation.
A scheme invests mostly in companies outside the top 250.
A small cap fund must hold at least 80% in the top 100.
Multi cap fund
A multi cap fund must invest at least 25% each in large, mid and small cap stocks, and at least 75% in equity overall.
A scheme must hold a quarter in each of three market-cap bands.
A multi cap fund can invest everything in large caps.
Flexi cap fund
A flexi cap fund invests at least 65% in equity with no restriction on market-cap allocation, so the manager can move across large, mid and small cap.
A scheme can shift freely between large and small companies.
A flexi cap fund must hold 25% in each market-cap band.
Focused fund
A focused fund invests in a maximum of 30 stocks and at least 65% in equity, taking concentrated positions.
A scheme holds just 25 stocks in its portfolio.
A focused fund holds more than 100 stocks.
ELSS
An Equity Linked Savings Scheme invests at least 80% in equity and has a three-year lock-in, and qualifies for the old tax regime deduction under Section 80C.

A scheme buys out-of-favour stocks believing they are undervalued.

An overnight fund invests in securities with a maturity of one day, so interest-rate and credit risk are very low.
A scheme holds paper that matures the next day.
An overnight fund holds bonds of ten years' maturity.

A scheme holds only paper maturing within three months.

A gilt fund invests mainly in low-rated corporate bonds.
Credit risk fund

A credit risk fund holds only AAA-rated bonds.

A scheme keeps 20% in equity and 80% in debt.

A fund buys a share in the cash market and sells its future at a higher price.

Selection criteria

units.title: Selecting the right investment products for investors
units.overview: Mutual funds are not the only product. This unit places them beside deposits, bonds, PPF, NPS, gold and insurance, so a distributor can recommend the right tool for the goal.
focus: Comparing mutual funds with other products on risk, return, liquidity and tax.
Matching products to goals and horizons.
facts: Fixed deposit
A bank fixed deposit pays a fixed rate for a fixed term; interest is taxable at slab rates, and premature withdrawal usually attracts a penalty.
An investor places money for two years at a known rate.
A fixed deposit offers returns linked to the stock market.
PPF
The Public Provident Fund is a government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year tenure and tax-free interest, with limited liquidity.
A saver locks money for fifteen years with government-backed safety.
PPF can be withdrawn in full at any time.
NPS
The National Pension System is a pension scheme regulated by PFRDA where contributions are invested in equity, corporate bonds and government securities and annuity is purchased on retirement.
A salaried person builds a retirement corpus with regulated pension fund managers.
NPS is a mutual fund regulated by SEBI.
Bonds and debentures
Bonds and debentures are debt securities paying periodic interest and returning principal at maturity; the issuer's credit rating drives their risk.
An investor lends to a company in return for coupons and the principal at maturity.
Bonds make the holder an owner of the company.
Gold
Gold is held as a hedge against inflation and uncertainty; it can be owned through physical gold, gold ETFs, sovereign gold bonds or gold funds.
An investor buys a gold ETF to avoid storage and purity worries.
Gold pays regular interest on holdings.
Real estate
Real estate offers potential for appreciation and rental income but is illiquid, needs large capital and has high transaction costs.
An investor finds it hard to sell a flat quickly at the right price.
Real estate is highly liquid and needs little capital.
Life insurance versus investment
Pure term insurance protects against loss of life; it should be separated from investment, and mutual funds are not insurance products.
A family buys a term plan for protection and invests separately for growth.
A mutual fund provides life cover.
Risk profiling
Risk profiling assesses a client's capacity and willingness to take risk through questions on age, income, dependants, goals and past behaviour, and guides product choice.
A distributor asks a client how he would feel if his investment fell 20%.
Risk profile is the same for every client of the same age.
Inflation
Inflation is the rise in prices over time, which erodes the purchasing power of money; investments must beat it to grow real wealth.
A saver's fixed return of 5% leaves little real gain when prices rise 6%.
Inflation increases the real value of cash.
Time horizon
The time horizon is the period for which money will be invested before it is needed; longer horizons can support more equity.
A client needing money in 6 months should avoid a high-equity scheme.
Time horizon has no effect on product choice.
Tax efficiency
The after-tax return matters more than the headline return; different products are taxed differently, so compare after-tax outcomes.
Two products with the same return leave different amounts after tax.
Only pre-tax returns matter in a comparison.
Capital protection
Mutual fund schemes do not protect capital; only specific instruments like bank deposits (up to the insured limit) and some government schemes offer greater safety.
A client wants assured safety of principal and is shown a deposit instead of an equity fund.
Mutual funds provide guaranteed capital protection.

units.title: Helping investors with financial planning
units.overview: Financial planning turns a product sale into a client relationship. This unit covers the planning process, goals, life stages, emergency funds and the discipline of reviewing.
facts: Financial plan
A financial plan is a documented roadmap that links the client's goals, resources, risk profile and time horizon to a set of actions.
A distributor prepares a written plan showing how each goal will be funded.
A financial plan is a list of schemes with last year's returns.
Goal-based planning
Goal-based planning sets investments against specific goals, such as a child's education, with a target amount, date and priority.
A client earmarks a separate investment for a house purchase in seven years.
Goal-based planning ignores timelines.
Emergency fund
An emergency fund is money kept in safe and liquid assets, usually three to six months of expenses, for unexpected needs.
A client keeps six months of living costs in a liquid fund.
An emergency fund should be invested in small-cap equity.
Life-cycle stage
A client's life stage, such as starting a career, raising a family or nearing retirement, shapes goals, risk capacity and asset allocation.
A 28-year-old and a 58-year-old need different mixes for the same sum.
Life stage has no effect on investment choices.
Risk capacity versus tolerance
Risk capacity is the ability to bear loss financially, while risk tolerance is willingness to bear it emotionally; advice should respect the lower of the two.
A wealthy client who panics at small losses has high capacity but low tolerance.
Risk tolerance and capacity are the same.
Time value of money
Money today is worth more than the same sum in the future because it can earn returns; planning must discount future needs and compound savings.
A client needs ₹50 lakh in 15 years and works out what to invest today.
A rupee today has the same value as a rupee in ten years.
Retirement planning
Retirement planning estimates the corpus needed to meet expenses after earning stops, allowing for inflation and longevity.
A client works out how much he must save each month to retire at 60.
Retirement planning needs no allowance for inflation.
Step-up SIP
A step-up SIP increases the instalment amount at regular intervals, usually yearly, in line with rising income.
An investor raises her SIP by 10% every year as her salary grows.
A step-up SIP reduces the instalment each year.
Periodic review
A plan should be reviewed at least once a year and on major life events, and rebalanced to the target allocation.
A client's portfolio is reviewed every year and after the birth of a child.
Once made, a plan never needs revisiting.

units.title: Recommending model portfolios and financial plans
units.overview: The final unit brings it together: building asset allocations for typical clients, using model portfolios, rebalancing and documenting advice responsibly.
visuals: These mixes show how allocation moves with risk. Real recommendations depend on the client's goals, horizon, capacity and tax position.
facts: Asset allocation
Asset allocation is the division of a portfolio among asset classes such as equity, debt and gold, and is the main driver of risk and return over time.
A client's portfolio is split 60% equity, 30% debt and 10% gold.
Asset allocation matters less than picking the best fund.
Strategic asset allocation
Strategic asset allocation sets long-term target weights based on the client's profile, which are maintained by periodic rebalancing.
A client's plan says 60% equity for the next ten years, whatever the news.
Strategic allocation changes with every market move.
Tactical asset allocation
Tactical allocation makes short-term deviations from the strategic weights to take advantage of market conditions.
A manager temporarily raises debt above target because equities look expensive.
Tactical allocation means never deviating from target.
Rebalancing
Rebalancing means bringing the portfolio back to its target allocation by selling what has grown too large and buying what has fallen behind.
Equity has risen to 70% of the portfolio against a 60% target, so some is sold.
Rebalancing means adding only to the best performer.
Core and satellite
A core and satellite approach holds the bulk of the portfolio in stable, low-cost funds and a smaller satellite part in higher-conviction ideas.
A portfolio holds 70% in index funds and 30% in a thematic fund.
Core and satellite means holding only satellite ideas.
Age-based rule of thumb
A rough guide sets equity at 100 minus the investor's age, adjusting for risk profile; it is a starting point, not a rule.
A 40-year-old starts discussing about 60% equity.
The rule fixes the exact equity percentage for everyone of a given age.
Glide path
A glide path gradually reduces equity and raises safer assets as a goal date approaches, to protect accumulated gains.
As a child's education nears, a family shifts from equity to debt funds.
A glide path raises equity as the goal date approaches.

A distributor files a signed risk profile and rationale for the recommended funds.
No written record of advice is needed.
Model portfolio
A model portfolio is a pre-defined allocation for a risk profile, used as a template and customised for the client.
A distributor shows a typical moderate-risk allocation as a starting point.
A model portfolio guarantees returns.
Conflict of interest
A conflict of interest arises when the distributor's earnings could bias the advice; it must be disclosed and managed in the client's favour.
A distributor discloses that one scheme pays him more but recommends the better fit for the client.
Conflicts of interest need not be disclosed.

mocks.w: Correct: An index fund or ETF replicates a market index, investing at least 95% in the index's securities, with low cost and no stock picking.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The AMFI Registration Number is a unique number issued to a distributor who has passed the NISM certification and follows the Code of Conduct. It must be renewed periodically.
o: Minor investor
Mid cap fund
Consolidated Account Statement (CAS)
ARN
mocks.w: ARN: The AMFI Registration Number is a unique number issued to a distributor who has passed the NISM certification and follows the Code of Conduct. It must be renewed periodically.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The National Pension System is a pension scheme regulated by PFRDA where contributions are invested in equity, corporate bonds and government securities and annuity is purchased on retirement.
o: Gilt fund
Custodian
NPS
ARN
mocks.w: NPS: The National Pension System is a pension scheme regulated by PFRDA where contributions are invested in equity, corporate bonds and government securities and annuity is purchased on retirement.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Risk-return trade-off”?
o: A distributor must disclose to the investor all commissions received from the AMC for the transaction, in a transparent manner.
Units must be allotted and refunds, if any, paid within five working days from the closure of the NFO.
Higher potential return generally comes with higher risk. Investors who want higher returns must accept greater volatility.
AMFI's Code of Conduct requires distributors to act honestly, disclose commissions, give suitable advice, and not mislead investors.
mocks.w: Risk-return trade-off: Higher potential return generally comes with higher risk. Investors who want higher returns must accept greater volatility.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Code of Conduct”?
o: Diversification means spreading investments across many securities, sectors or asset classes so that a fall in one has a limited effect on the whole portfolio.
AMFI's Code of Conduct requires distributors to act honestly, disclose commissions, give suitable advice, and not mislead investors.
SEBI groups schemes into equity, debt, hybrid, solution oriented and other categories with defined definitions, and each AMC may offer only one scheme per category, with a few exceptions.
A lien is a charge marked on units, for example when pledged as security for a loan, so they cannot be redeemed until the lien is removed.
mocks.w: Code of Conduct: AMFI's Code of Conduct requires distributors to act honestly, disclose commissions, give suitable advice, and not mislead investors.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Total expense ratio (TER)” is correct?
o: IDCW is tax-free in the hands of all investors.
TER is deducted separately from the investor's bank account.
TER is the annual percentage of a scheme's average assets charged for management, distribution and operating costs, and it is reflected in the daily NAV.
A distributor needs no registration to sell mutual funds.
mocks.w: Correct: TER is the annual percentage of a scheme's average assets charged for management, distribution and operating costs, and it is reflected in the daily NAV.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Stamp duty on units” is correct?
o: Stamp duty is charged at 0.005% on the purchase of mutual fund units, including switches and SIP instalments.
A nominee becomes the permanent legal owner of the units.
Stamp duty is charged on units only when redeemed.
The sponsor need not contribute to the AMC's net worth.
mocks.w: Correct: Stamp duty is charged at 0.005% on the purchase of mutual fund units, including switches and SIP instalments.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Modified duration” is correct?
o: A switch has no tax or load implications.
Modified duration estimates the percentage change in a bond's price for a 1% change in yield. A higher duration means more interest-rate sensitivity.
Duration measures the credit rating of the bond.
The SID contains only the fund house's history.
mocks.w: Correct: Modified duration estimates the percentage change in a bond's price for a 1% change in yield. A higher duration means more interest-rate sensitivity.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “KYC”?
o: A change of bank details needs a written request with proof of the new bank and is checked by the RTA; some schemes impose a cooling-off for large redemptions.
A flexi cap fund invests at least 65% in equity with no restriction on market-cap allocation, so the manager can move across large, mid and small cap.
Know Your Customer is mandatory for all mutual fund investors. It verifies identity and address, and the records are kept with a KYC registration agency.
The SID states the proportion of the scheme's assets to be held in each asset class and the permissible ranges, which are binding on the fund manager.
mocks.w: KYC: Know Your Customer is mandatory for all mutual fund investors. It verifies identity and address, and the records are kept with a KYC registration agency.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? A plan should be reviewed at least once a year and on major life events, and rebalanced to the target allocation.
o: Time value of money
Asset allocation
Liquidity risk
Periodic review
mocks.w: Periodic review: A plan should be reviewed at least once a year and on major life events, and rebalanced to the target allocation.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Transmission is the transfer of units to the legal heirs or surviving holders on the death of a holder, supported by documents like the death certificate.
o: Arbitrage fund
Interest rate risk
Cut-off time
Transmission
mocks.w: Transmission: Transmission is the transfer of units to the legal heirs or surviving holders on the death of a holder, supported by documents like the death certificate.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Risk profiling” is correct?
o: Risk profiling assesses a client's capacity and willingness to take risk through questions on age, income, dependants, goals and past behaviour, and guides product choice.
An arbitrage fund takes a large one-sided view on stocks.
Risk profile is the same for every client of the same age.
An interval scheme lets investors transact on any day.
mocks.w: Correct: Risk profiling assesses a client's capacity and willingness to take risk through questions on age, income, dependants, goals and past behaviour, and guides product choice.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? A change of bank details needs a written request with proof of the new bank and is checked by the RTA; some schemes impose a cooling-off for large redemptions.
o: Periodic review
Value and contra funds
Change of bank details
Applicable NAV
mocks.w: Change of bank details: A change of bank details needs a written request with proof of the new bank and is checked by the RTA; some schemes impose a cooling-off for large redemptions.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Time value of money” is correct?
o: A rupee today has the same value as a rupee in ten years.
Money today is worth more than the same sum in the future because it can earn returns; planning must discount future needs and compound savings.
A fixed deposit offers returns linked to the stock market.
IDCW is extra money that does not reduce NAV.
mocks.w: Correct: Money today is worth more than the same sum in the future because it can earn returns; planning must discount future needs and compound savings.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Risk capacity is the ability to bear loss financially, while risk tolerance is willingness to bear it emotionally; advice should respect the lower of the two.
o: Absolute return
Portfolio disclosure
Risk-return trade-off
Risk capacity versus tolerance
mocks.w: Risk capacity versus tolerance: Risk capacity is the ability to bear loss financially, while risk tolerance is willingness to bear it emotionally; advice should respect the lower of the two.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Retirement planning estimates the corpus needed to meet expenses after earning stops, allowing for inflation and longevity.
o: Dividend or IDCW payout timeline
Custodian
Retirement planning
Interval scheme
mocks.w: Retirement planning: Retirement planning estimates the corpus needed to meet expenses after earning stops, allowing for inflation and longevity.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? A value fund follows a value strategy, and a contra fund follows a contrarian one, each investing at least 65% in equity; a fund house can offer only one of these two.
o: Value and contra funds
NPS
Sponsor
Ex-dividend NAV effect
mocks.w: Value and contra funds: A value fund follows a value strategy, and a contra fund follows a contrarian one, each investing at least 65% in equity; a fund house can offer only one of these two.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Equity-oriented fund” is correct?
o: A switch has no tax or load implications.
For tax purposes, an equity-oriented fund invests at least 65% of its assets in equity shares of domestic companies.
An open-ended scheme can be redeemed only on maturity.
A scheme with 40% equity is equity-oriented.
mocks.w: Correct: For tax purposes, an equity-oriented fund invests at least 65% of its assets in equity shares of domestic companies.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Equity valuation” is correct?
o: A value fund buys only stocks at record highs.
A small cap fund must hold at least 80% in the top 100.
Listed equity shares are valued at the closing price on the principal stock exchange on the valuation day.
Shares are valued at the price at which they were bought.
mocks.w: Correct: Listed equity shares are valued at the closing price on the principal stock exchange on the valuation day.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The distributor should record the client's profile, the recommendation and the reasons, and obtain the client's acknowledgement to show suitability.
o: Trustees
Documenting advice
CAGR
Goal-based planning
mocks.w: Documenting advice: The distributor should record the client's profile, the recommendation and the reasons, and obtain the client's acknowledgement to show suitability.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Scheme-specific risk factors” is correct?
o: The offer document lists the risks specific to the scheme, such as credit risk for debt schemes, so that investors make informed decisions.
Risk factors are required only for equity schemes.
Last year's top performer is always the best choice.
An emergency fund should be invested in small-cap equity.
mocks.w: Correct: The offer document lists the risks specific to the scheme, such as credit risk for debt schemes, so that investors make informed decisions.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Debt valuation”?
o: Retirement and children's funds have a lock-in of five years or until retirement age or the child turns 18, whichever is earlier.
Debt securities are valued at prices provided by SEBI-approved valuation agencies appointed by AMFI, to ensure uniform valuation across funds.
Stamp duty is charged at 0.005% on the purchase of mutual fund units, including switches and SIP instalments.
A plan should be reviewed at least once a year and on major life events, and rebalanced to the target allocation.
mocks.w: Debt valuation: Debt securities are valued at prices provided by SEBI-approved valuation agencies appointed by AMFI, to ensure uniform valuation across funds.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Sponsor” is correct?
o: The sponsor is the person or entity that sets up the mutual fund and establishes the trust. It must meet SEBI's track-record and net-worth conditions.
The sponsor manages the investments of each scheme day to day.
ELSS has a lock-in of one year.
High returns can be earned without any additional risk.
mocks.w: Correct: The sponsor is the person or entity that sets up the mutual fund and establishes the trust. It must meet SEBI's track-record and net-worth conditions.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Trail commission”?
o: The NAV applied to a transaction depends on the cut-off time and when the funds are available for use by the scheme, not just when the application is made.
Trail commission is paid to a distributor as long as the investor stays invested, usually as a percentage of the assets he has brought in.
The sponsor is the person or entity that sets up the mutual fund and establishes the trust. It must meet SEBI's track-record and net-worth conditions.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India is the statutory regulator that registers and regulates mutual funds and protects investors under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.
mocks.w: Trail commission: Trail commission is paid to a distributor as long as the investor stays invested, usually as a percentage of the assets he has brought in.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Alpha” is correct?
o: Solution-oriented funds have no lock-in.
A negative alpha shows outperformance.
A price index is the preferred benchmark because it includes dividends.
Alpha is the excess return of a fund over what its risk (beta) would predict, showing the value added by the fund manager.
mocks.w: Correct: Alpha is the excess return of a fund over what its risk (beta) would predict, showing the value added by the fund manager.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.
o: Large cap fund
Churning
Redemption timeline
Capital protection
mocks.w: Churning: Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Rupee cost averaging” is correct?
o: Rupee cost averaging means a fixed amount buys more units when NAV is low and fewer when it is high, lowering the average cost per unit over time.
Rupee cost averaging ensures there will never be a loss.
A lien means the units have been sold.
The NAV applied is always the one on the day of the cheque.
mocks.w: Correct: Rupee cost averaging means a fixed amount buys more units when NAV is low and fewer when it is high, lowering the average cost per unit over time.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Ex-dividend NAV effect” is correct?
o: KYC is required only for investments above ₹10 lakh.
Mutual funds provide guaranteed capital protection.
When an IDCW is paid, the scheme's NAV falls by the amount paid, so the investor's wealth is unchanged before tax.
IDCW is extra money that does not reduce NAV.
mocks.w: Correct: When an IDCW is paid, the scheme's NAV falls by the amount paid, so the investor's wealth is unchanged before tax.

mocks.p: Which statement about “SEBI SCORES / ODR” is correct?
o: A focused fund holds more than 100 stocks.
Complaints against AMCs can be made only to the sponsor.
Investors can file complaints against AMCs and intermediaries through SEBI's complaint system, and use the online dispute resolution platform if not satisfied.
IDCW is extra money that does not reduce NAV.
mocks.w: Correct: Investors can file complaints against AMCs and intermediaries through SEBI's complaint system, and use the online dispute resolution platform if not satisfied.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Professional management” is correct?
o: A corporate bond fund holds mostly AA-rated and below paper.
Professional management means a qualified fund manager and research team select and monitor securities for the scheme, for a fee charged as part of the expense ratio.
Professional management guarantees returns above the market.
An arbitrage fund takes a large one-sided view on stocks.
mocks.w: Correct: Professional management means a qualified fund manager and research team select and monitor securities for the scheme, for a fee charged as part of the expense ratio.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Step-up SIP” is correct?
o: A large cap fund invests mainly in companies ranked 251 onwards.
XIRR can be used only for lump-sum investments.
A step-up SIP reduces the instalment each year.
A step-up SIP increases the instalment amount at regular intervals, usually yearly, in line with rising income.
mocks.w: Correct: A step-up SIP increases the instalment amount at regular intervals, usually yearly, in line with rising income.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Corporate bond fund”?
o: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is the statutory regulator that registers and regulates mutual funds and protects investors under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.
Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.
A corporate bond fund invests at least 80% in the highest-rated (AA+ and above) corporate bonds.
A person cannot be both a registered investment adviser and a distributor for the same client; roles and fees must be kept clearly separate to avoid conflicts of interest.
mocks.w: Corporate bond fund: A corporate bond fund invests at least 80% in the highest-rated (AA+ and above) corporate bonds.

mocks.p: Which statement about “AMFI” is correct?
o: A negative alpha shows outperformance.
The Association of Mutual Funds in India is the industry body of AMCs. It sets best practices, issues the ARN to distributors, and publishes the daily NAVs.
An arbitrage fund takes a large one-sided view on stocks.
AMFI makes the laws that bind mutual funds.
mocks.w: Correct: The Association of Mutual Funds in India is the industry body of AMCs. It sets best practices, issues the ARN to distributors, and publishes the daily NAVs.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Folio”?
o: A folio is the account number allotted by an AMC to an investor, under which all that investor's units in that fund house are recorded.
Absolute return is the percentage change in value over a period, ignoring how long it took. It is (end value − start value) ÷ start value.
Exit load is a charge levied when units are redeemed within a stated period. It is credited to the scheme, not kept by the AMC.
When an IDCW is paid, the scheme's NAV falls by the amount paid, so the investor's wealth is unchanged before tax.
mocks.w: Folio: A folio is the account number allotted by an AMC to an investor, under which all that investor's units in that fund house are recorded.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Suitability” is correct?
o: The KIM replaces the need for any offer document.
Suitability means recommending a product that fits the client's goals, risk profile, time horizon and financial situation.
Suitability is determined only by the scheme's past return.
The only channel to buy mutual funds is a bank branch.
mocks.w: Correct: Suitability means recommending a product that fits the client's goals, risk profile, time horizon and financial situation.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Inflation” is correct?
o: Inflation increases the real value of cash.
A mid cap fund invests mainly in the top 100 companies.
Inflation is the rise in prices over time, which erodes the purchasing power of money; investments must beat it to grow real wealth.
Solution-oriented funds have no lock-in.
mocks.w: Correct: Inflation is the rise in prices over time, which erodes the purchasing power of money; investments must beat it to grow real wealth.

mocks.p: Which statement about “New Fund Offer (NFO)” is correct?
o: Fund houses are not required to publish their holdings.
An NFO is the initial offer of a new scheme's units to the public. The offer period cannot exceed 15 days.
An NFO can stay open for six months.
Solution-oriented funds have no lock-in.
mocks.w: Correct: An NFO is the initial offer of a new scheme's units to the public. The offer period cannot exceed 15 days.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The Sharpe ratio is the excess return over the risk-free rate per unit of standard deviation. A higher ratio means better risk-adjusted performance.
o: IDCW taxation
Large cap fund
Sharpe ratio
EUIN
mocks.w: Sharpe ratio: The Sharpe ratio is the excess return over the risk-free rate per unit of standard deviation. A higher ratio means better risk-adjusted performance.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Documenting advice”?
o: Gains on equity-oriented funds held over 12 months are taxed at 12.5% on the amount above ₹1.25 lakh in a financial year.
AMFI's Code of Conduct requires distributors to act honestly, disclose commissions, give suitable advice, and not mislead investors.
Transmission is the transfer of units to the legal heirs or surviving holders on the death of a holder, supported by documents like the death certificate.
The distributor should record the client's profile, the recommendation and the reasons, and obtain the client's acknowledgement to show suitability.
mocks.w: Documenting advice: The distributor should record the client's profile, the recommendation and the reasons, and obtain the client's acknowledgement to show suitability.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? A good selection looks at risk-adjusted return, consistency over several periods, expense ratio, portfolio quality, fund manager continuity and fit with the investor's profile.
o: Selection criteria
Disclosure of commission
Ex-dividend NAV effect
Trail commission
mocks.w: Selection criteria: A good selection looks at risk-adjusted return, consistency over several periods, expense ratio, portfolio quality, fund manager continuity and fit with the investor's profile.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Slab-wise TER” is correct?
o: A focused fund holds more than 100 stocks.
The maximum TER rises as the scheme grows.
A switch has no tax or load implications.
SEBI sets maximum TER slabs that fall as a scheme's assets under management grow, so larger schemes charge a lower percentage.
mocks.w: Correct: SEBI sets maximum TER slabs that fall as a scheme's assets under management grow, so larger schemes charge a lower percentage.

mocks.p: Which statement about “STT” is correct?
o: STT is charged on every purchase of mutual fund units.
KYC is required only for investments above ₹10 lakh.
Securities Transaction Tax is levied on the redemption of equity-oriented fund units; there is no STT on purchase, and none on debt funds.
A gilt fund invests mainly in low-rated corporate bonds.
mocks.w: Correct: Securities Transaction Tax is levied on the redemption of equity-oriented fund units; there is no STT on purchase, and none on debt funds.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “NPS”?
o: A corporate bond fund invests at least 80% in the highest-rated (AA+ and above) corporate bonds.
A direct plan is bought directly from the AMC without a distributor, so no commission is paid and the expense ratio is lower.
The National Pension System is a pension scheme regulated by PFRDA where contributions are invested in equity, corporate bonds and government securities and annuity is purchased on retirement.
The fund accountant maintains the scheme's books and computes NAV, while auditors independently audit the accounts.
mocks.w: NPS: The National Pension System is a pension scheme regulated by PFRDA where contributions are invested in equity, corporate bonds and government securities and annuity is purchased on retirement.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? A conservative hybrid fund invests 10% to 25% in equity and 75% to 90% in debt.
o: Conservative hybrid fund
Riskometer
Gilt fund
Time horizon
mocks.w: Conservative hybrid fund: A conservative hybrid fund invests 10% to 25% in equity and 75% to 90% in debt.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Transparency” is correct?
o: Mutual funds disclose NAV daily, portfolios monthly and factsheets regularly, so investors can see where their money is invested.
Fund houses are not required to publish their holdings.
A price index is the preferred benchmark because it includes dividends.
A mid cap fund invests mainly in the top 100 companies.
mocks.w: Correct: Mutual funds disclose NAV daily, portfolios monthly and factsheets regularly, so investors can see where their money is invested.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Lien” is correct?
o: A lien means the units have been sold.
A lien is a charge marked on units, for example when pledged as security for a loan, so they cannot be redeemed until the lien is removed.
Suitability is determined only by the scheme's past return.
AMFI makes the laws that bind mutual funds.
mocks.w: Correct: A lien is a charge marked on units, for example when pledged as security for a loan, so they cannot be redeemed until the lien is removed.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Small cap fund”?
o: Money today is worth more than the same sum in the future because it can earn returns; planning must discount future needs and compound savings.
A Systematic Withdrawal Plan redeems a fixed amount of units at regular intervals, giving the investor a regular cash flow.
A small cap fund invests at least 65% in companies ranked 251 and below by market capitalisation.
A client's life stage, such as starting a career, raising a family or nearing retirement, shapes goals, risk capacity and asset allocation.
mocks.w: Small cap fund: A small cap fund invests at least 65% in companies ranked 251 and below by market capitalisation.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Scheme Information Document (SID)”?
o: An overnight fund invests in securities with a maturity of one day, so interest-rate and credit risk are very low.
The SID contains scheme-specific details: investment objective, asset allocation, strategy, risk factors, load structure, benchmark and fees.
A regular plan is bought through a distributor, who is paid a commission from the scheme's expense ratio, making its expense ratio higher than the direct plan's.
SEBI has banned upfront commission to distributors; commissions are now paid on a trail basis, to align the distributor's interest with the investor's.
mocks.w: Scheme Information Document (SID): The SID contains scheme-specific details: investment objective, asset allocation, strategy, risk factors, load structure, benchmark and fees.

mocks.p: A scheme holds just 25 stocks in its portfolio. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Multi cap fund
Focused fund
Value and contra funds
Arbitrage fund
mocks.w: This is Focused fund. A focused fund invests in a maximum of 30 stocks and at least 65% in equity, taking concentrated positions.

mocks.p: A scheme can shift freely between large and small companies. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Flexi cap fund
Solution-oriented funds
Focused fund
Index fund and ETF
mocks.w: This is Flexi cap fund. A flexi cap fund invests at least 65% in equity with no restriction on market-cap allocation, so the manager can move across large, mid and small cap.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The riskometer shows a scheme's risk on six levels: low, low to moderate, moderate, moderately high, high and very high, and is updated based on portfolio risk.
o: Cash investment limit
KYC
Riskometer
Fundamental attribute change
mocks.w: Riskometer: The riskometer shows a scheme's risk on six levels: low, low to moderate, moderate, moderately high, high and very high, and is updated based on portfolio risk.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Cut-off time” is correct?
o: Applications received at 6 pm get the same day's NAV.
A folio is a type of scheme.
The NAV applied is always the one on the day of the cheque.
The cut-off time is the time of day by which a valid application with funds must be received to get that day's NAV. For most schemes it is 3:00 pm.
mocks.w: Correct: The cut-off time is the time of day by which a valid application with funds must be received to get that day's NAV. For most schemes it is 3:00 pm.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? An open-ended scheme accepts purchases and redemptions at NAV on every business day after launch and has no fixed maturity.
o: Transparency
Open-ended scheme
Liquidity
Diversification
mocks.w: Open-ended scheme: An open-ended scheme accepts purchases and redemptions at NAV on every business day after launch and has no fixed maturity.

mocks.p: An investor updates the registered bank account with supporting proof. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Lien
Nomination
Change of bank details
Switch
mocks.w: This is Change of bank details. A change of bank details needs a written request with proof of the new bank and is checked by the RTA; some schemes impose a cooling-off for large redemptions.

mocks.p: A family buys a term plan for protection and invests separately for growth. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Time horizon
Bonds and debentures
NPS
Life insurance versus investment
mocks.w: This is Life insurance versus investment. Pure term insurance protects against loss of life; it should be separated from investment, and mutual funds are not insurance products.

mocks.p: Which statement about “PPF” is correct?
o: PPF can be withdrawn in full at any time.
The Public Provident Fund is a government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year tenure and tax-free interest, with limited liquidity.
Only pre-tax returns matter in a comparison.
Real estate is highly liquid and needs little capital.
mocks.w: Correct: The Public Provident Fund is a government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year tenure and tax-free interest, with limited liquidity.

mocks.p: Which statement about “STP” is correct?
o: An SWP is a plan to buy units regularly.
An STP moves money to the investor's bank account.
A Systematic Transfer Plan transfers a fixed amount at regular intervals from one scheme to another within the same fund house.
IDCW can be dispatched any time within six months.
mocks.w: Correct: A Systematic Transfer Plan transfers a fixed amount at regular intervals from one scheme to another within the same fund house.

mocks.p: A distributor checks a client's horizon and risk tolerance before suggesting a scheme. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Distributor channels
Direct plan
Suitability
Regular plan
mocks.w: This is Suitability. Suitability means recommending a product that fits the client's goals, risk profile, time horizon and financial situation.

mocks.p: An investor sells an equity fund after eight months and pays the short-term rate. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: LTCG on equity funds
STCG on equity funds
Exit load
Ex-dividend NAV effect
mocks.w: This is STCG on equity funds. Gains on equity-oriented funds sold within 12 months are short-term and taxed at 20%.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The Securities and Exchange Board of India is the statutory regulator that registers and regulates mutual funds and protects investors under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.
o: Scheme categorisation
Product labelling
SEBI
Stamp duty on units
mocks.w: SEBI: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is the statutory regulator that registers and regulates mutual funds and protects investors under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Alpha is the excess return of a fund over what its risk (beta) would predict, showing the value added by the fund manager.
o: XIRR
Credit risk
Total Return Index (TRI)
Alpha
mocks.w: Alpha: Alpha is the excess return of a fund over what its risk (beta) would predict, showing the value added by the fund manager.

mocks.p: An investor receives one statement showing all her funds from different fund houses. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Applicable NAV
Consolidated Account Statement (CAS)
SWP
Change of bank details
mocks.w: This is Consolidated Account Statement (CAS). A single statement covering all of an investor's mutual fund holdings across AMCs, sent monthly if there were transactions, otherwise half-yearly.

mocks.p: A scheme's cover page displays a dial pointing to very high. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Stamp duty on units
Riskometer
Cash investment limit
Product labelling
mocks.w: This is Riskometer. The riskometer shows a scheme's risk on six levels: low, low to moderate, moderate, moderately high, high and very high, and is updated based on portfolio risk.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Model portfolio” is correct?
o: Conflicts of interest need not be disclosed.
A model portfolio is a pre-defined allocation for a risk profile, used as a template and customised for the client.
A model portfolio guarantees returns.
Rebalancing means adding only to the best performer.
mocks.w: Correct: A model portfolio is a pre-defined allocation for a risk profile, used as a template and customised for the client.

mocks.p: A scheme pays ₹2 per unit and its NAV drops by ₹2 the same day. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Ex-dividend NAV effect
STCG on equity funds
Equity-oriented fund
Total expense ratio (TER)
mocks.w: This is Ex-dividend NAV effect. When an IDCW is paid, the scheme's NAV falls by the amount paid, so the investor's wealth is unchanged before tax.

mocks.p: An investor holds units in the same account as her shares. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Change of bank details
Demat mode
Dividend or IDCW payout timeline
SWP
mocks.w: This is Demat mode. Mutual fund units can be held in dematerialised form with a depository participant, in addition to a statement of account from the AMC.

mocks.p: An investor assumes a ₹10 unit is cheaper than a ₹50 unit in another scheme. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Allotment timeline
New Fund Offer (NFO)
Scheme Information Document (SID)
NFO price
mocks.w: This is NFO price. Units in an NFO are typically offered at ₹10 each, with no assurance that this is a better price than existing schemes' NAV.

mocks.p: An investor invests ₹5,000 on the 5th of every month into the same scheme. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: STP
SIP
Joint holding modes
Dividend or IDCW payout timeline
mocks.w: This is SIP. A Systematic Investment Plan invests a fixed amount at regular intervals, which averages the purchase cost and builds discipline.

mocks.p: An investor wants to know the scheme's asset allocation and exit load before investing. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Scheme Information Document (SID)
NFO price
Statement of Additional Information (SAI)
Allotment timeline
mocks.w: This is Scheme Information Document (SID). The SID contains scheme-specific details: investment objective, asset allocation, strategy, risk factors, load structure, benchmark and fees.

mocks.p: An agency updates investor folios and dispatches account statements. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA)
Custodian
Sponsor
Fund accountant and auditor
mocks.w: This is Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA). The RTA maintains unit holders' records, processes purchases and redemptions, and sends statements on behalf of the AMC.

mocks.p: An investor sells units today and expects to receive money in a few working days. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Minor investor
Redemption timeline
Demat mode
Consolidated Account Statement (CAS)
mocks.w: This is Redemption timeline. Redemption proceeds must generally be paid within three working days of the transaction date for most schemes; liquid funds may be quicker.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Conflict of interest” is correct?
o: Conflicts of interest need not be disclosed.
The rule fixes the exact equity percentage for everyone of a given age.
A conflict of interest arises when the distributor's earnings could bias the advice; it must be disclosed and managed in the client's favour.
A model portfolio guarantees returns.
mocks.w: Correct: A conflict of interest arises when the distributor's earnings could bias the advice; it must be disclosed and managed in the client's favour.
