mocks.w: Correct: The SID states the proportion of the scheme's assets to be held in each asset class and the permissible ranges, which are binding on the fund manager.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Churning” is correct?
o: Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.
Trail commission is paid only once, on the day of investing.
Churning benefits the investor through lower costs.
Commissions are confidential and need not be disclosed.
mocks.w: Correct: Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Risk profiling assesses a client's capacity and willingness to take risk through questions on age, income, dependants, goals and past behaviour, and guides product choice.
The after-tax return matters more than the headline return; different products are taxed differently, so compare after-tax outcomes.
Mutual fund schemes do not protect capital; only specific instruments like bank deposits (up to the insured limit) and some government schemes offer greater safety.
NPS is a mutual fund regulated by SEBI.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The National Pension System is a pension scheme regulated by PFRDA where contributions are invested in equity, corporate bonds and government securities and annuity is purchased on retirement.

mocks.p: A scheme must hold a quarter in each of three market-cap bands. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Mid cap fund
Conservative hybrid fund
Gilt fund
Multi cap fund
mocks.w: This is Multi cap fund. A multi cap fund must invest at least 25% each in large, mid and small cap stocks, and at least 75% in equity overall.

mocks.p: Which statement about “NAV calculation” is correct?
o: NAV equals the market value of the scheme's assets less its liabilities, divided by units outstanding, and is declared every business day.
NAV is declared once a week.
A debt fund held beyond three years gets indexation benefit.
A scheme with 40% equity is equity-oriented.
mocks.w: Correct: NAV equals the market value of the scheme's assets less its liabilities, divided by units outstanding, and is declared every business day.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An investor can invest in cash in a mutual fund up to ₹50,000 per investor per mutual fund per financial year.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India is the statutory regulator that registers and regulates mutual funds and protects investors under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.
Stamp duty is charged at 0.005% on the purchase of mutual fund units, including switches and SIP instalments.
Product labels are optional for equity schemes.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Each scheme's cover and advertisements must describe the product in plain language: what the scheme is, suited for whom, and what risk level applies.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Mutual fund schemes do not protect capital; only specific instruments like bank deposits (up to the insured limit) and some government schemes offer greater safety.
Only pre-tax returns matter in a comparison.
Risk profiling assesses a client's capacity and willingness to take risk through questions on age, income, dependants, goals and past behaviour, and guides product choice.
Inflation is the rise in prices over time, which erodes the purchasing power of money; investments must beat it to grow real wealth.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The after-tax return matters more than the headline return; different products are taxed differently, so compare after-tax outcomes.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Applicable NAV” is correct?
o: The NAV applied to a transaction depends on the cut-off time and when the funds are available for use by the scheme, not just when the application is made.
The NAV applied is always the one on the day of the cheque.
In 'anyone or survivor' mode all holders must sign each redemption.
A folio is a type of scheme.
mocks.w: Correct: The NAV applied to a transaction depends on the cut-off time and when the funds are available for use by the scheme, not just when the application is made.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A nominee becomes the permanent legal owner of the units.
A switch is moving investment from one scheme to another, or between plans or options in the same scheme; it is treated as redemption and fresh purchase.
The NAV applied to a transaction depends on the cut-off time and when the funds are available for use by the scheme, not just when the application is made.
A change of bank details needs a written request with proof of the new bank and is checked by the RTA; some schemes impose a cooling-off for large redemptions.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Nomination lets a holder name a person who will receive the units on the holder's death. Nominees are not the legal owners; they hold the proceeds for the legal heirs.

mocks.p: Which statement about “STCG on equity funds” is correct?
o: Gains on equity-oriented funds sold within 12 months are short-term and taxed at 20%.
Long-term equity gains are taxed from the first rupee.
A debt fund held beyond three years gets indexation benefit.
Short-term equity gains are exempt from tax.
mocks.w: Correct: Gains on equity-oriented funds sold within 12 months are short-term and taxed at 20%.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Mutual funds publish portfolios of all schemes monthly on their websites and with AMFI, and publish the half-yearly financial results.
A change in a scheme's fundamental attributes needs a written notice to unit holders and an exit option at the prevailing NAV without exit load for at least 30 days.
The riskometer shows a scheme's risk on six levels: low, low to moderate, moderate, moderately high, high and very high, and is updated based on portfolio risk.
An EUIN is allotted to every investor on investing.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The Employee Unique Identification Number identifies the individual employee or relationship manager who advises on a transaction, even when an ARN of the firm is used.

mocks.p: A person tries to invest ₹80,000 in cash in one fund house in a year. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Cash investment limit
AMFI
SEBI SCORES / ODR
SEBI
mocks.w: This is Cash investment limit. An investor can invest in cash in a mutual fund up to ₹50,000 per investor per mutual fund per financial year.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Periodic review” is correct?
o: Once made, a plan never needs revisiting.
An emergency fund should be invested in small-cap equity.
A plan should be reviewed at least once a year and on major life events, and rebalanced to the target allocation.
Goal-based planning ignores timelines.
mocks.w: Correct: A plan should be reviewed at least once a year and on major life events, and rebalanced to the target allocation.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Transmission is the transfer of units to the legal heirs or surviving holders on the death of a holder, supported by documents like the death certificate.
An SWP is a plan to buy units regularly.
Payout of IDCW must be dispatched within seven working days of the record date.
A lien is a charge marked on units, for example when pledged as security for a loan, so they cannot be redeemed until the lien is removed.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A Systematic Withdrawal Plan redeems a fixed amount of units at regular intervals, giving the investor a regular cash flow.

mocks.p: A scheme holds mostly central and state government bonds. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Flexi cap fund
Selection criteria
Gilt fund
Overnight fund
mocks.w: This is Gilt fund. A gilt fund invests at least 80% in government securities across maturities, so credit risk is negligible but interest-rate risk can be high.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Fundamental attribute change” is correct?
o: A change in a scheme's fundamental attributes needs a written notice to unit holders and an exit option at the prevailing NAV without exit load for at least 30 days.
KYC is required only for investments above ₹10 lakh.
Fund houses can change fundamental attributes without informing investors.
Complaints against AMCs can be made only to the sponsor.
mocks.w: Correct: A change in a scheme's fundamental attributes needs a written notice to unit holders and an exit option at the prevailing NAV without exit load for at least 30 days.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Churning benefits the investor through lower costs.
A regular plan is bought through a distributor, who is paid a commission from the scheme's expense ratio, making its expense ratio higher than the direct plan's.
A person cannot be both a registered investment adviser and a distributor for the same client; roles and fees must be kept clearly separate to avoid conflicts of interest.
A direct plan is bought directly from the AMC without a distributor, so no commission is paid and the expense ratio is lower.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.

mocks.p: ₹500,000 grows to ₹661,250 in 2 years. What is the CAGR, approximately?
mocks.w: CAGR = (end ÷ start)^(1/2) − 1 ≈ 15%.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: All mutual fund units can be encashed instantly at any hour.
Mutual funds disclose NAV daily, portfolios monthly and factsheets regularly, so investors can see where their money is invested.
An open-ended scheme accepts purchases and redemptions at NAV on every business day after launch and has no fixed maturity.
Professional management means a qualified fund manager and research team select and monitor securities for the scheme, for a fee charged as part of the expense ratio.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Liquidity in mutual funds means that units of open-ended schemes can be redeemed on any business day at the applicable NAV, subject to exit loads and settlement time.

mocks.p: An investor invests ₹75,000 in a scheme when the applicable NAV is ₹12.5. Ignoring charges, how many units are allotted?
An investor invests ₹75,000 in a scheme when the applicable NAV is ₹32.5. Ignoring charges, how many units are allotted?
A fund tends to rise 12% when the market rises 10%. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Yield to maturity (YTM)
Liquidity risk
Beta
XIRR
mocks.w: This is Beta. Beta measures a fund's sensitivity to the market. A beta of 1.2 means it is expected to move 20% more than the market.

mocks.p: A fund house sets up its mutual fund as a registered public trust. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Mutual fund as a trust
Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA)
Sponsor
Fund accountant and auditor
mocks.w: This is Mutual fund as a trust. In India a mutual fund is constituted as a public trust under the Indian Trusts Act, and the trust is registered with SEBI.

mocks.p: A scheme chases higher yield by lending to lower-rated companies. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Index fund and ETF
Value and contra funds
Credit risk fund
Flexi cap fund
mocks.w: This is Credit risk fund. A credit risk fund invests at least 65% in corporate bonds rated AA and below, seeking higher yields at higher credit risk.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A financial plan is a documented roadmap that links the client's goals, resources, risk profile and time horizon to a set of actions.
An emergency fund is money kept in safe and liquid assets, usually three to six months of expenses, for unexpected needs.
A rupee today has the same value as a rupee in ten years.
Risk capacity is the ability to bear loss financially, while risk tolerance is willingness to bear it emotionally; advice should respect the lower of the two.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Money today is worth more than the same sum in the future because it can earn returns; planning must discount future needs and compound savings.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: NAV is the per-unit value of a scheme: total market value of its assets less its liabilities, divided by the number of units outstanding.
Fund houses are not required to publish their holdings.
Mutual fund investments are subject to market risk. The value of units can rise and fall, and past performance does not assure future results.
A closed-ended scheme has a fixed maturity and units are bought during the NFO only; investors exit at maturity or by selling on a stock exchange where listed.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Mutual funds disclose NAV daily, portfolios monthly and factsheets regularly, so investors can see where their money is invested.

mocks.p: An index fund drifts a little from its index return every year. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Tracking error
Interest rate risk
Risk-return trade-off
Liquidity risk
mocks.w: This is Tracking error. Tracking error is the standard deviation of the difference between an index fund's return and its benchmark's. A lower figure means closer replication.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The RTA maintains unit holders' records, processes purchases and redemptions, and sends statements on behalf of the AMC.
The fund accountant maintains the scheme's books and computes NAV, while auditors independently audit the accounts.
The custodian safekeeps the securities and settles the trades of the schemes, and is independent of the sponsor.
The AMC holds the securities of the schemes.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The AMC is appointed by the trustees to manage the schemes' investments and operations. At least half of its directors must be independent of the sponsor.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Mutual fund schemes do not protect capital; only specific instruments like bank deposits (up to the insured limit) and some government schemes offer greater safety.
Real estate is highly liquid and needs little capital.
Gold is held as a hedge against inflation and uncertainty; it can be owned through physical gold, gold ETFs, sovereign gold bonds or gold funds.
The Public Provident Fund is a government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year tenure and tax-free interest, with limited liquidity.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Real estate offers potential for appreciation and rental income but is illiquid, needs large capital and has high transaction costs.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A person cannot be both a registered investment adviser and a distributor for the same client; roles and fees must be kept clearly separate to avoid conflicts of interest.
AMCs carry out due diligence on distributors and check that their ARN, certification and code compliance are valid before accepting business.
A regular plan has the same expense ratio as the direct plan.
A distributor must disclose to the investor all commissions received from the AMC for the transaction, in a transparent manner.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A regular plan is bought through a distributor, who is paid a commission from the scheme's expense ratio, making its expense ratio higher than the direct plan's.

mocks.p: A scheme has assets of ₹520 crore, liabilities of ₹20 crore and 25 crore units, so this is ₹20. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Unit
Open-ended scheme
Diversification
Net Asset Value (NAV)
mocks.w: This is Net Asset Value (NAV). NAV is the per-unit value of a scheme: total market value of its assets less its liabilities, divided by the number of units outstanding.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A model portfolio guarantees returns.
A glide path gradually reduces equity and raises safer assets as a goal date approaches, to protect accumulated gains.
Asset allocation is the division of a portfolio among asset classes such as equity, debt and gold, and is the main driver of risk and return over time.
A core and satellite approach holds the bulk of the portfolio in stable, low-cost funds and a smaller satellite part in higher-conviction ideas.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A model portfolio is a pre-defined allocation for a risk profile, used as a template and customised for the client.

mocks.p: A scheme with average assets of ₹5000 crore has a total expense ratio of 0.5%. What is the annual expense charged to the scheme?
o: ₹25 crore
₹15.79 crore
₹27.5 crore
₹22.15 crore
mocks.w: 0.5% of ₹5000 crore = ₹25 crore.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A good selection looks at risk-adjusted return, consistency over several periods, expense ratio, portfolio quality, fund manager continuity and fit with the investor's profile.
A large cap fund invests at least 80% of its assets in the top 100 companies by market capitalisation.
An index fund or ETF replicates a market index, investing at least 95% in the index's securities, with low cost and no stock picking.
A thematic fund is well diversified across all sectors.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A sectoral or thematic fund invests at least 80% in a particular sector or theme, such as banking or technology, and carries concentration risk.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A switch is moving investment from one scheme to another, or between plans or options in the same scheme; it is treated as redemption and fresh purchase.
A lien means the units have been sold.
Transmission is the transfer of units to the legal heirs or surviving holders on the death of a holder, supported by documents like the death certificate.
A minor's folio is operated by a guardian, and when the minor turns 18 a fresh KYC is needed, and the guardian's operation stops.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A lien is a charge marked on units, for example when pledged as security for a loan, so they cannot be redeemed until the lien is removed.

mocks.p: An investor runs a monthly SIP of ₹10,000 for 24 months. What is the total amount invested?
Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A lien is a charge marked on units, for example when pledged as security for a loan, so they cannot be redeemed until the lien is removed.
A Systematic Withdrawal Plan redeems a fixed amount of units at regular intervals, giving the investor a regular cash flow.
Mutual fund units can never be held in demat form.
A folio is the account number allotted by an AMC to an investor, under which all that investor's units in that fund house are recorded.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Mutual fund units can be held in dematerialised form with a depository participant, in addition to a statement of account from the AMC.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An aggressive hybrid fund invests 65% to 80% in equity and 20% to 35% in debt.
Last year's top performer is always the best choice.
A credit risk fund invests at least 65% in corporate bonds rated AA and below, seeking higher yields at higher credit risk.
A conservative hybrid fund invests 10% to 25% in equity and 75% to 90% in debt.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A good selection looks at risk-adjusted return, consistency over several periods, expense ratio, portfolio quality, fund manager continuity and fit with the investor's profile.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The Employee Unique Identification Number identifies the individual employee or relationship manager who advises on a transaction, even when an ARN of the firm is used.
Complaints against AMCs can be made only to the sponsor.
A change in a scheme's fundamental attributes needs a written notice to unit holders and an exit option at the prevailing NAV without exit load for at least 30 days.
The riskometer shows a scheme's risk on six levels: low, low to moderate, moderate, moderately high, high and very high, and is updated based on portfolio risk.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Investors can file complaints against AMCs and intermediaries through SEBI's complaint system, and use the online dispute resolution platform if not satisfied.

mocks.p: An investor invests ₹120,000 in a scheme when the applicable NAV is ₹32.5. Ignoring charges, how many units are allotted?
An investor's long-term capital gain from equity-oriented funds in a year is ₹325,000 (no other gains). At 12.5% above the ₹1.25 lakh exemption, what is the tax (ignoring cess)?
An investor runs a monthly SIP of ₹2,000 for 12 months. What is the total amount invested?
Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A rough guide sets equity at 100 minus the investor's age, adjusting for risk profile; it is a starting point, not a rule.
Strategic allocation changes with every market move.
The distributor should record the client's profile, the recommendation and the reasons, and obtain the client's acknowledgement to show suitability.
Tactical allocation makes short-term deviations from the strategic weights to take advantage of market conditions.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Strategic asset allocation sets long-term target weights based on the client's profile, which are maintained by periodic rebalancing.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Real estate offers potential for appreciation and rental income but is illiquid, needs large capital and has high transaction costs.
PPF can be withdrawn in full at any time.
The time horizon is the period for which money will be invested before it is needed; longer horizons can support more equity.
Pure term insurance protects against loss of life; it should be separated from investment, and mutual funds are not insurance products.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The Public Provident Fund is a government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year tenure and tax-free interest, with limited liquidity.

mocks.p: An investor bought units at NAV ₹20. One year later the NAV is ₹26 after an IDCW of ₹2 per unit was paid. What is the return including the payout?
Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An open-ended scheme accepts purchases and redemptions at NAV on every business day after launch and has no fixed maturity.
Professional management means a qualified fund manager and research team select and monitor securities for the scheme, for a fee charged as part of the expense ratio.
Each unit always stays worth ₹10.
A mutual fund is a trust that pools money from many investors and invests it in securities such as shares and bonds, managed by professionals for the benefit of unit holders.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A unit is the smallest share of a mutual fund scheme's portfolio that an investor owns. The number of units held shows the investor's proportional ownership.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An arbitrage fund invests at least 65% in equity and equity-related instruments and profits from price differences between cash and futures markets; it is taxed as equity.
A conservative hybrid fund invests 10% to 25% in equity and 75% to 90% in debt.
A value fund follows a value strategy, and a contra fund follows a contrarian one, each investing at least 65% in equity; a fund house can offer only one of these two.
A gilt fund invests mainly in low-rated corporate bonds.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A gilt fund invests at least 80% in government securities across maturities, so credit risk is negligible but interest-rate risk can be high.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Gains on equity-oriented funds sold within 12 months are short-term and taxed at 20%.
Each AMC values bonds as it sees fit.
A specified mutual fund invests more than 65% in debt and money-market instruments. Gains on units bought from April 2023 are taxed at the investor's slab rate regardless of holding period.
NAV equals the market value of the scheme's assets less its liabilities, divided by units outstanding, and is declared every business day.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Debt securities are valued at prices provided by SEBI-approved valuation agencies appointed by AMFI, to ensure uniform valuation across funds.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Bonds and debentures are debt securities paying periodic interest and returning principal at maturity; the issuer's credit rating drives their risk.
Risk profiling assesses a client's capacity and willingness to take risk through questions on age, income, dependants, goals and past behaviour, and guides product choice.
Inflation is the rise in prices over time, which erodes the purchasing power of money; investments must beat it to grow real wealth.
Time horizon has no effect on product choice.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The time horizon is the period for which money will be invested before it is needed; longer horizons can support more equity.

mocks.p: A distributor cannot take a lump sum at the time of purchase. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Trail commission
Mis-selling
Churning
Upfront commission
mocks.w: This is Upfront commission. SEBI has banned upfront commission to distributors; commissions are now paid on a trail basis, to align the distributor's interest with the investor's.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The riskometer shows a scheme's risk on six levels: low, low to moderate, moderate, moderately high, high and very high, and is updated based on portfolio risk.
Each scheme's cover and advertisements must describe the product in plain language: what the scheme is, suited for whom, and what risk level applies.
Fund houses can change fundamental attributes without informing investors.
Know Your Customer is mandatory for all mutual fund investors. It verifies identity and address, and the records are kept with a KYC registration agency.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A change in a scheme's fundamental attributes needs a written notice to unit holders and an exit option at the prevailing NAV without exit load for at least 30 days.

mocks.p: A SIP invests ₹1000 each month at NAVs of ₹50, ₹40, ₹50. What is the average cost per unit?
mocks.w: Total ₹3000 ÷ 65 units = ₹46.15. Because fixed money buys more units when NAV is low, the cost per unit is below the simple average of NAVs.

mocks.p: At stamp duty of 0.005% on purchases, how much stamp duty applies to a purchase of ₹200,000?
Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Mutual funds publish portfolios of all schemes monthly on their websites and with AMFI, and publish the half-yearly financial results.
Know Your Customer is mandatory for all mutual fund investors. It verifies identity and address, and the records are kept with a KYC registration agency.
The riskometer has only three levels: low, medium and high.
The Employee Unique Identification Number identifies the individual employee or relationship manager who advises on a transaction, even when an ARN of the firm is used.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The riskometer shows a scheme's risk on six levels: low, low to moderate, moderate, moderately high, high and very high, and is updated based on portfolio risk.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The RTA calculates the portfolio's investment strategy.
The AMC is appointed by the trustees to manage the schemes' investments and operations. At least half of its directors must be independent of the sponsor.
The fund accountant maintains the scheme's books and computes NAV, while auditors independently audit the accounts.
The custodian safekeeps the securities and settles the trades of the schemes, and is independent of the sponsor.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The RTA maintains unit holders' records, processes purchases and redemptions, and sends statements on behalf of the AMC.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A conflict of interest arises when the distributor's earnings could bias the advice; it must be disclosed and managed in the client's favour.
A core and satellite approach holds the bulk of the portfolio in stable, low-cost funds and a smaller satellite part in higher-conviction ideas.
Rebalancing means bringing the portfolio back to its target allocation by selling what has grown too large and buying what has fallen behind.
Tactical allocation means never deviating from target.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Tactical allocation makes short-term deviations from the strategic weights to take advantage of market conditions.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Higher potential return generally comes with higher risk. Investors who want higher returns must accept greater volatility.
Absolute return is the percentage change in value over a period, ignoring how long it took. It is (end value − start value) ÷ start value.
Tracking error is the standard deviation of the difference between an index fund's return and its benchmark's. A lower figure means closer replication.
CAGR is the simple average of each year's return.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Compound Annual Growth Rate is the constant yearly rate at which an investment would have grown to reach its final value, used for periods over one year.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A credit risk fund invests at least 65% in corporate bonds rated AA and below, seeking higher yields at higher credit risk.
An overnight fund invests in securities with a maturity of one day, so interest-rate and credit risk are very low.
A gilt fund invests at least 80% in government securities across maturities, so credit risk is negligible but interest-rate risk can be high.
ELSS has a lock-in of one year.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: An Equity Linked Savings Scheme invests at least 80% in equity and has a three-year lock-in, and qualifies for the old tax regime deduction under Section 80C.

mocks.p: A scheme with a three-year maturity lets investors in only during the launch period. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Unit
Closed-ended scheme
Economies of scale
Open-ended scheme
mocks.w: This is Closed-ended scheme. A closed-ended scheme has a fixed maturity and units are bought during the NFO only; investors exit at maturity or by selling on a stock exchange where listed.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The fund manager can ignore the stated asset allocation.
The offer document lists the risks specific to the scheme, such as credit risk for debt schemes, so that investors make informed decisions.
The SID contains scheme-specific details: investment objective, asset allocation, strategy, risk factors, load structure, benchmark and fees.
Units in an NFO are typically offered at ₹10 each, with no assurance that this is a better price than existing schemes' NAV.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The SID states the proportion of the scheme's assets to be held in each asset class and the permissible ranges, which are binding on the fund manager.

mocks.p: A purchase made before cut-off but with funds credited next day takes the later day's NAV. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Applicable NAV
Switch
Rupee cost averaging
Folio
mocks.w: This is Applicable NAV. The NAV applied to a transaction depends on the cut-off time and when the funds are available for use by the scheme, not just when the application is made.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An NFO is the initial offer of a new scheme's units to the public. The offer period cannot exceed 15 days.
The SID states the proportion of the scheme's assets to be held in each asset class and the permissible ranges, which are binding on the fund manager.
The offer document lists the risks specific to the scheme, such as credit risk for debt schemes, so that investors make informed decisions.
The SAI contains details of only a single scheme.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The SAI holds information common to the fund house and all its schemes: constitution, sponsor, trustees, AMC, service providers and legal details.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.
A person cannot be both a registered investment adviser and a distributor for the same client; roles and fees must be kept clearly separate to avoid conflicts of interest.
Suitability means recommending a product that fits the client's goals, risk profile, time horizon and financial situation.
Trail commission is paid only once, on the day of investing.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Trail commission is paid to a distributor as long as the investor stays invested, usually as a percentage of the assets he has brought in.

mocks.p: An investor bought units at NAV ₹25. One year later the NAV is ₹27 after an IDCW of ₹2 per unit was paid. What is the return including the payout?
An investor runs a monthly SIP of ₹10,000 for 60 months. What is the total amount invested?
A client's plan says 60% equity for the next ten years, whatever the news. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Strategic asset allocation
Tactical asset allocation
Core and satellite
Model portfolio
mocks.w: This is Strategic asset allocation. Strategic asset allocation sets long-term target weights based on the client's profile, which are maintained by periodic rebalancing.

mocks.p: An investor sells equity-oriented fund units after 8 months, with a short-term gain of ₹100,000. At 20% short-term capital gains tax (ignoring cess), how much tax is payable?
A scheme holds only paper maturing within three months. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Liquid fund
Aggressive hybrid fund
Multi cap fund
Gilt fund
mocks.w: This is Liquid fund. A liquid fund invests in debt and money-market securities with a maturity of up to 91 days.

mocks.p: A scheme's documents say it is suited to investors seeking long-term growth and carries very high risk. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Code of Conduct
Product labelling
Scheme categorisation
Fundamental attribute change
mocks.w: This is Product labelling. Each scheme's cover and advertisements must describe the product in plain language: what the scheme is, suited for whom, and what risk level applies.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An emergency fund is money kept in safe and liquid assets, usually three to six months of expenses, for unexpected needs.
Retirement planning needs no allowance for inflation.
A financial plan is a documented roadmap that links the client's goals, resources, risk profile and time horizon to a set of actions.
Risk capacity is the ability to bear loss financially, while risk tolerance is willingness to bear it emotionally; advice should respect the lower of the two.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Retirement planning estimates the corpus needed to meet expenses after earning stops, allowing for inflation and longevity.

mocks.p: An investor invests ₹10,000 in a scheme when the applicable NAV is ₹25. Ignoring charges, how many units are allotted?
An investor places money for two years at a known rate. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: PPF
Bonds and debentures
Risk profiling
Fixed deposit
mocks.w: This is Fixed deposit. A bank fixed deposit pays a fixed rate for a fixed term; interest is taxable at slab rates, and premature withdrawal usually attracts a penalty.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: When an IDCW is paid, the scheme's NAV falls by the amount paid, so the investor's wealth is unchanged before tax.
Gains on equity-oriented funds sold within 12 months are short-term and taxed at 20%.
Shares are valued at the price at which they were bought.
A specified mutual fund invests more than 65% in debt and money-market instruments. Gains on units bought from April 2023 are taxed at the investor's slab rate regardless of holding period.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Listed equity shares are valued at the closing price on the principal stock exchange on the valuation day.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Asset allocation matters less than picking the best fund.
Strategic asset allocation sets long-term target weights based on the client's profile, which are maintained by periodic rebalancing.
A model portfolio is a pre-defined allocation for a risk profile, used as a template and customised for the client.
Rebalancing means bringing the portfolio back to its target allocation by selling what has grown too large and buying what has fallen behind.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Asset allocation is the division of a portfolio among asset classes such as equity, debt and gold, and is the main driver of risk and return over time.

mocks.p: An investor bought units at NAV ₹25. One year later the NAV is ₹31 after an IDCW of ₹1 per unit was paid. What is the return including the payout?
Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: When interest rates rise, the prices of existing bonds fall and vice versa, which affects debt fund NAVs, especially of longer-duration funds.
Compound Annual Growth Rate is the constant yearly rate at which an investment would have grown to reach its final value, used for periods over one year.
Beta measures a fund's sensitivity to the market. A beta of 1.2 means it is expected to move 20% more than the market.
Duration measures the credit rating of the bond.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Modified duration estimates the percentage change in a bond's price for a 1% change in yield. A higher duration means more interest-rate sensitivity.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: SEBI sets maximum TER slabs that fall as a scheme's assets under management grow, so larger schemes charge a lower percentage.
Gains on equity-oriented funds sold within 12 months are short-term and taxed at 20%.
IDCW is extra money that does not reduce NAV.
Debt securities are valued at prices provided by SEBI-approved valuation agencies appointed by AMFI, to ensure uniform valuation across funds.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: When an IDCW is paid, the scheme's NAV falls by the amount paid, so the investor's wealth is unchanged before tax.

mocks.p: A scheme holds mostly bonds of top-rated companies. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Corporate bond fund
Selection criteria
Flexi cap fund
Multi cap fund
mocks.w: This is Corporate bond fund. A corporate bond fund invests at least 80% in the highest-rated (AA+ and above) corporate bonds.

mocks.p: Two products with the same return leave different amounts after tax. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Gold
Real estate
Risk profiling
Tax efficiency
mocks.w: This is Tax efficiency. The after-tax return matters more than the headline return; different products are taxed differently, so compare after-tax outcomes.

mocks.p: An investor runs a monthly SIP of ₹2,000 for 36 months. What is the total amount invested?
Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Goal-based planning ignores timelines.
A client's life stage, such as starting a career, raising a family or nearing retirement, shapes goals, risk capacity and asset allocation.
Retirement planning estimates the corpus needed to meet expenses after earning stops, allowing for inflation and longevity.
A step-up SIP increases the instalment amount at regular intervals, usually yearly, in line with rising income.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Goal-based planning sets investments against specific goals, such as a child's education, with a target amount, date and priority.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Standard deviation measures how much a fund's returns vary around its average. A higher figure means more volatility.
When interest rates rise, the prices of existing bonds fall and vice versa, which affects debt fund NAVs, especially of longer-duration funds.
Modified duration estimates the percentage change in a bond's price for a 1% change in yield. A higher duration means more interest-rate sensitivity.
XIRR can be used only for lump-sum investments.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: XIRR is the annualised return when there are multiple cash flows on different dates, such as SIP instalments.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A value fund buys only stocks at record highs.
An Equity Linked Savings Scheme invests at least 80% in equity and has a three-year lock-in, and qualifies for the old tax regime deduction under Section 80C.
A liquid fund invests in debt and money-market securities with a maturity of up to 91 days.
A small cap fund invests at least 65% in companies ranked 251 and below by market capitalisation.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A value fund follows a value strategy, and a contra fund follows a contrarian one, each investing at least 65% in equity; a fund house can offer only one of these two.

mocks.p: An investor wanting equity-like returns must accept bigger swings in value. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Risk-return trade-off
Beta
Modified duration
Absolute return
mocks.w: This is Risk-return trade-off. Higher potential return generally comes with higher risk. Investors who want higher returns must accept greater volatility.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: AMFI makes the laws that bind mutual funds.
AMFI's Code of Conduct requires distributors to act honestly, disclose commissions, give suitable advice, and not mislead investors.
The riskometer shows a scheme's risk on six levels: low, low to moderate, moderate, moderately high, high and very high, and is updated based on portfolio risk.
The AMFI Registration Number is a unique number issued to a distributor who has passed the NISM certification and follows the Code of Conduct. It must be renewed periodically.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The Association of Mutual Funds in India is the industry body of AMCs. It sets best practices, issues the ARN to distributors, and publishes the daily NAVs.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Retirement and children's funds have a lock-in of five years or until retirement age or the child turns 18, whichever is earlier.
A small cap fund invests at least 65% in companies ranked 251 and below by market capitalisation.
An overnight fund invests in securities with a maturity of one day, so interest-rate and credit risk are very low.
A focused fund holds more than 100 stocks.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A focused fund invests in a maximum of 30 stocks and at least 65% in equity, taking concentrated positions.

mocks.p: An AMC checks that the distributor's registration is valid before paying commission. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Disclosure of commission
Know Your Distributor
Segregation of roles
Mis-selling
mocks.w: This is Know Your Distributor. AMCs carry out due diligence on distributors and check that their ARN, certification and code compliance are valid before accepting business.

mocks.p: A bond's expected return if held until it matures is called its yield. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Total Return Index (TRI)
Yield to maturity (YTM)
Credit risk
Standard deviation
mocks.w: This is Yield to maturity (YTM). YTM is the annualised return earned if a bond is held to maturity and all coupons are reinvested at the same rate.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Bonds and debentures are debt securities paying periodic interest and returning principal at maturity; the issuer's credit rating drives their risk.
A bank fixed deposit pays a fixed rate for a fixed term; interest is taxable at slab rates, and premature withdrawal usually attracts a penalty.
Inflation increases the real value of cash.
The Public Provident Fund is a government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year tenure and tax-free interest, with limited liquidity.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Inflation is the rise in prices over time, which erodes the purchasing power of money; investments must beat it to grow real wealth.

mocks.p: A distributor sells a high-risk equity fund to a retired client who needs safety by promising assured returns. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Mis-selling
Churning
Trail commission
Upfront commission
mocks.w: This is Mis-selling. Mis-selling is selling a product that is unsuitable for the client or by misrepresenting its features, risk or returns.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: AMFI is the statutory regulator of mutual funds.
Know Your Customer is mandatory for all mutual fund investors. It verifies identity and address, and the records are kept with a KYC registration agency.
An investor can invest in cash in a mutual fund up to ₹50,000 per investor per mutual fund per financial year.
SEBI groups schemes into equity, debt, hybrid, solution oriented and other categories with defined definitions, and each AMC may offer only one scheme per category, with a few exceptions.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is the statutory regulator that registers and regulates mutual funds and protects investors under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.

mocks.p: The NFO closes and units are allotted a few working days later. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: NFO price
Asset allocation pattern
Statement of Additional Information (SAI)
Allotment timeline
mocks.w: This is Allotment timeline. Units must be allotted and refunds, if any, paid within five working days from the closure of the NFO.

mocks.p: A short summary document is attached to the application form. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Scheme Information Document (SID)
Key Information Memorandum (KIM)
Asset allocation pattern
Scheme-specific risk factors
mocks.w: This is Key Information Memorandum (KIM). The KIM is a short summary of the SID and SAI given with the application form so investors see the essentials first. SEBI has since moved towards a standard scheme summary document with the same purpose.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The fund accountant maintains the scheme's books and computes NAV, while auditors independently audit the accounts.
The sponsor must contribute at least 40% of the net worth of the AMC.
Trustees decide which stocks the schemes buy.
In India a mutual fund is constituted as a public trust under the Indian Trusts Act, and the trust is registered with SEBI.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Trustees hold the fund's property in trust for unit holders and supervise the AMC. At least two-thirds of the trustees must be independent of the sponsor.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Suitability means recommending a product that fits the client's goals, risk profile, time horizon and financial situation.
An adviser can charge a fee and also take commission from the same client.
Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.
SEBI has banned upfront commission to distributors; commissions are now paid on a trail basis, to align the distributor's interest with the investor's.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A person cannot be both a registered investment adviser and a distributor for the same client; roles and fees must be kept clearly separate to avoid conflicts of interest.

mocks.p: A scheme has net assets of ₹1200 crore before deducting liabilities of ₹30 crore. It has 25 crore units outstanding. What is the NAV per unit?
mocks.w: NAV = (₹1200 − ₹30) crore ÷ 25 crore units = ₹46.8.

mocks.p: Equity has risen to 70% of the portfolio against a 60% target, so some is sold. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Core and satellite
Strategic asset allocation
Model portfolio
Rebalancing
mocks.w: This is Rebalancing. Rebalancing means bringing the portfolio back to its target allocation by selling what has grown too large and buying what has fallen behind.

mocks.p: A distributor discloses that one scheme pays him more but recommends the better fit for the client. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Glide path
Conflict of interest
Tactical asset allocation
Core and satellite
mocks.w: This is Conflict of interest. A conflict of interest arises when the distributor's earnings could bias the advice; it must be disclosed and managed in the client's favour.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A rough guide sets equity at 100 minus the investor's age, adjusting for risk profile; it is a starting point, not a rule.
A glide path gradually reduces equity and raises safer assets as a goal date approaches, to protect accumulated gains.
Core and satellite means holding only satellite ideas.
Tactical allocation makes short-term deviations from the strategic weights to take advantage of market conditions.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A core and satellite approach holds the bulk of the portfolio in stable, low-cost funds and a smaller satellite part in higher-conviction ideas.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Inflation is the rise in prices over time, which erodes the purchasing power of money; investments must beat it to grow real wealth.
The Public Provident Fund is a government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year tenure and tax-free interest, with limited liquidity.
Risk profiling assesses a client's capacity and willingness to take risk through questions on age, income, dependants, goals and past behaviour, and guides product choice.
Bonds make the holder an owner of the company.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Bonds and debentures are debt securities paying periodic interest and returning principal at maturity; the issuer's credit rating drives their risk.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Applications received at 6 pm get the same day's NAV.
A change of bank details needs a written request with proof of the new bank and is checked by the RTA; some schemes impose a cooling-off for large redemptions.
A single statement covering all of an investor's mutual fund holdings across AMCs, sent monthly if there were transactions, otherwise half-yearly.
A minor's folio is operated by a guardian, and when the minor turns 18 a fresh KYC is needed, and the guardian's operation stops.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The cut-off time is the time of day by which a valid application with funds must be received to get that day's NAV. For most schemes it is 3:00 pm.

mocks.p: A scheme holding 70% in domestic shares qualifies for equity tax treatment. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Equity-oriented fund
Slab-wise TER
IDCW taxation
STCG on equity funds
mocks.w: This is Equity-oriented fund. For tax purposes, an equity-oriented fund invests at least 65% of its assets in equity shares of domestic companies.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The Association of Mutual Funds in India is the industry body of AMCs. It sets best practices, issues the ARN to distributors, and publishes the daily NAVs.
Mutual funds publish portfolios of all schemes monthly on their websites and with AMFI, and publish the half-yearly financial results.
KYC is required only for investments above ₹10 lakh.
SEBI groups schemes into equity, debt, hybrid, solution oriented and other categories with defined definitions, and each AMC may offer only one scheme per category, with a few exceptions.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Know Your Customer is mandatory for all mutual fund investors. It verifies identity and address, and the records are kept with a KYC registration agency.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Suitability is determined only by the scheme's past return.
Churning is persuading an investor to frequently switch schemes mainly to earn the distributor more commission, with little or no benefit to the investor.
A regular plan is bought through a distributor, who is paid a commission from the scheme's expense ratio, making its expense ratio higher than the direct plan's.
AMCs carry out due diligence on distributors and check that their ARN, certification and code compliance are valid before accepting business.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Suitability means recommending a product that fits the client's goals, risk profile, time horizon and financial situation.

mocks.p: An investor finds it hard to sell a flat quickly at the right price. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Inflation
Life insurance versus investment
Real estate
Time horizon
mocks.w: This is Real estate. Real estate offers potential for appreciation and rental income but is illiquid, needs large capital and has high transaction costs.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A Systematic Withdrawal Plan redeems a fixed amount of units at regular intervals, giving the investor a regular cash flow.
A switch is moving investment from one scheme to another, or between plans or options in the same scheme; it is treated as redemption and fresh purchase.
Rupee cost averaging ensures there will never be a loss.
A change of bank details needs a written request with proof of the new bank and is checked by the RTA; some schemes impose a cooling-off for large redemptions.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Rupee cost averaging means a fixed amount buys more units when NAV is low and fewer when it is high, lowering the average cost per unit over time.

mocks.p: A distributor asks a client how he would feel if his investment fell 20%. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Risk profiling
Inflation
Tax efficiency
PPF
mocks.w: This is Risk profiling. Risk profiling assesses a client's capacity and willingness to take risk through questions on age, income, dependants, goals and past behaviour, and guides product choice.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Risk capacity is the ability to bear loss financially, while risk tolerance is willingness to bear it emotionally; advice should respect the lower of the two.
A plan should be reviewed at least once a year and on major life events, and rebalanced to the target allocation.
Life stage has no effect on investment choices.
A financial plan is a documented roadmap that links the client's goals, resources, risk profile and time horizon to a set of actions.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A client's life stage, such as starting a career, raising a family or nearing retirement, shapes goals, risk capacity and asset allocation.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An NFO is the initial offer of a new scheme's units to the public. The offer period cannot exceed 15 days.
Units must be allotted and refunds, if any, paid within five working days from the closure of the NFO.
The SAI holds information common to the fund house and all its schemes: constitution, sponsor, trustees, AMC, service providers and legal details.
The KIM replaces the need for any offer document.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The KIM is a short summary of the SID and SAI given with the application form so investors see the essentials first. SEBI has since moved towards a standard scheme summary document with the same purpose.

mocks.p: A scheme invests mostly in companies outside the top 250. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Multi cap fund
Small cap fund
Arbitrage fund
Conservative hybrid fund
mocks.w: This is Small cap fund. A small cap fund invests at least 65% in companies ranked 251 and below by market capitalisation.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The Employee Unique Identification Number identifies the individual employee or relationship manager who advises on a transaction, even when an ARN of the firm is used.
An investor can invest in cash in a mutual fund up to ₹50,000 per investor per mutual fund per financial year.
A distributor needs no registration to sell mutual funds.
Know Your Customer is mandatory for all mutual fund investors. It verifies identity and address, and the records are kept with a KYC registration agency.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The AMFI Registration Number is a unique number issued to a distributor who has passed the NISM certification and follows the Code of Conduct. It must be renewed periodically.

mocks.p: An investor runs a monthly SIP of ₹10,000 for 12 months. What is the total amount invested?
An investor redeems units worth ₹120,000 within the exit-load period, where the exit load is 0.5%. What amount is deducted as exit load?
A fund house opens subscription for a newly launched scheme for two weeks. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Key Information Memorandum (KIM)
Scheme-specific risk factors
Asset allocation pattern
New Fund Offer (NFO)
mocks.w: This is New Fund Offer (NFO). An NFO is the initial offer of a new scheme's units to the public. The offer period cannot exceed 15 days.

mocks.p: An investor sees a tiny deduction at the time units are allotted. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Stamp duty on units
Cash investment limit
AMFI
SEBI
mocks.w: This is Stamp duty on units. Stamp duty is charged at 0.005% on the purchase of mutual fund units, including switches and SIP instalments.

mocks.p: A bank's relationship manager's own code is entered on the investor's form. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: EUIN
Cash investment limit
Fundamental attribute change
Scheme categorisation
mocks.w: This is EUIN. The Employee Unique Identification Number identifies the individual employee or relationship manager who advises on a transaction, even when an ARN of the firm is used.
